We are telling Cisco how to work differently, using the tools and best practices that we see.  We will learn together.  We get to take simplification and speed to another level.  Every demographic in the workplace can join in to reboot work.  In this digital world the walls must come down, employees must work together to solve problems, motivate each other and bring in the talent to continue the wave.  It is real - Cisco is doing it!  We are connecting everything, benefiting everyone and innovating everywhere!  The culture at Cisco is evolving...Human Resources is standing up in a bold way to be a driving force in how the company evolves.  We all have to step into the conversation and be a part of this change.  Relationships still matter but you also have to think differently - real time.  Nothing remains the same....this is fantastic.

Pros:
I was always afraid of joining a behemoth of a company: afraid to lose my creativity and individuality. Of course, you're a small fish in a large ocean at Cisco, but I've come to realize/understand that everything (your enjoyment, focus, motivation, loyalty, and on and on) hinges directly on the business unit (BU) and managing chain you're brought into. I was extremely fortunate to have landed in an up-and-coming BU that is constantly heralded as a "do not fail" BU which really keeps you positive. If anything, do your homework and talk to multiple people that work directly in or with your team under the same direct chain of management and pray you'll not be working under an old-school type that refuses to learn new technologies and practices. Some of those guys refuse to accept that it's 2016 and the world has moved on :) Below are some things I find great about working here (keeping in mind both my manager and director are wicked smart and easy-going if you're a hard worker and can prove you're a solid engineer):

* a fantastic work from home policy - I refuse to uproot my family and slog it out in CA where home prices are 4-5x more, so I get an income that basically no other local company can match in overall compensation without moving more into the senior manager/VP positions
* benefits are great - my family uses the high deductible plan which works well for us if you can build up enough buffer in your HSA and take advantage of the hundreds of dollars of HSA  incentives; paid life insurance; paid short- and long-term disability
* structured bonus plan - the bonus is nothing to laugh at and is extremely welcome; it's tied to both your performance (kind of derived by your manager) and the companies metrics (customer service quality, shareholders, revenue, etc) but if both do well your percentage goes up
* 4.5% match, immediately vested, 401k-roth option, brokerage option, bonus matching, bonus stock (4-year vesting)
* BU-dependent, but budget for training, conferences, books, classes, etc are all very good if you choose to use them
* perks galore - I guess I didn't realize that with thousands of employees comes greater purchasing power, so various discounts on anything from Whirlpool appliances and movie tickets, to reduced cell phone bills and (I kid you not) solar panel installs. You may not use all of what's available or even care, but to even provide so many different ways to save you cash on things you're going to buy will lead to more compensation
* the career path and income increases in all former jobs has been engineer, senior engineer, (maybe principal), manager, glass ceiling...then what? More management? At Cisco they have two paths: management and engineering. The roles and responsibilities increase as you go up levels in either of those paths, as well as the pay and perks, however, they understand that good engineers may want to remain engineers, and they reward their great ones accordingly. I think this is in my top 3.
Cons:
* Kind of an ongoing reorganization (aka, forced layoffs) discussion that seems to have been a strong theme the last few years, but nothing really negative as happened yet. I believe there's a severance package if this does happen to you?
* Like many places, your peers could be complete duds, which forces you to pick up their slack or else the entire team including yourself look terrible...but, without any "real" guidelines in place to let these people go they kind of hang around and leach off the company and their peers
* I've been here over a year and through various conversations with my peers I've discovered that I should probably be a level above where I'm at now, however it is not really clear at all how you move up

Pros:
This is a great sales training rotational program for people with sales experience who want to first learn about and understand the Customer Success role. Cisco in general is an amazing company to work for and our leaders are just that; intelligent, committed, individuals who strive to ensure our success.

Customer Success is the new era of sales and I would highly reccomend this position. This role is unique in how it exposes you to the new way of not just selling products, but selling business outcomes. It's also exciting for those who like to innovate, value relationship-building with the customer, and pioneer new processes and ideas. I really enjoy being able to have direct impact at a company this big and being a member of the Customer Success Team here at Cisco gives you that unique opportunity. 

I can't emphasize enough the responsiveness of our executives and leaders; I'm honestly amazed at how Cisco has given new employees the ability to have exposure with our senior management and how willing and compasionate they are about our sales team.

I would reccomend Cisco, Customer Success, and Sales to anyone, hands down.

Working at a fortune 100 company as large as Cisco, especially as we migrate our revenue model and product offerings, means there will be holes. I think this is natural at any large company but the mindset of adapting to ever-changing processes, acquisitions, etc. is crucial in order to thrive. Not necessarily a con if you like a challenge and put in a lot of effort. 

No "work from home" but not necessarily a con either; I personally prefer to come in the office but just something to keep in mind as people have different views on this.

Pros:
I started working at Cisco immediately after graduating college. I was placed in operations and was able to learn some valuable generic business skills. Although the role wasn't necessarily a good long term fit for me, I was able to find a new job within Cisco IT after about 2 weeks of looking for something new. This new role has been amazing! I have a manager who is flexible with my work hours, coworkers who are fun and hard-working, and work that makes me feel fulfilled. Every time I talk to my family about my job and work/life balance, they are amazed and advise I stay at Cisco for as long as I can. I believe I am paid well for my status of early in career and I am learning a lot of skills that will be beneficial in whichever line of work I do. Management is great and I feel that out of the three managers I've had, each one of them were attentive to my personal and career growth. 

I have not had any experience at other corporate workplaces, but I know that I have fallen in love with the culture of Cisco. I feel as if this is a safe place with no judgments, people who care about you, and provides an open work environment. Definitely a great place to work and I highly recommend!
Cons:
Cisco is a large company and therefore, it can sometimes take a while to get things done due to red tape. I personally have not encountered this problem yet but have heard stories. 

Even though I am lucky to be on a team with an average age of about 26, many people who work at Cisco are a little older (or wiser). As an early and career worker, it can sometimes be difficult to relate to those who are 20+ years older than I am but that doesn't mean they are any less nice.

Pros:
Joining as a graduate and having been part of other graduate roles with other companies that I won't name, Cisco really devotes a lot of time to training and developing their employees. The interview process did not accurately reflect the culture that lies within Cisco, one that truely cares and provides meaningful work.

As someone who struggled with the quarter life crisis, wondering if a terrible 9-5 job for the rest of my life in 'mundane corporate' doing pretty much nothing but pretending to look busy whilst shuffling numbers on spreadsheets or doing meaningless presentations no one cares about, Cisco definitely changed my perspective on corporate life.

The work is meaningful, it gives me purpose, and whilst it is challenging, you are adequately rewarded and then some. The people are excellent and if you are passionate about technology, this is the place to be. A moral and ethical company, I strongly feel that Cisco is a great place to work. I highly recommend to anyone who were overachievers in high school and university who feel like their talent is wasted at other companies to apply to Cisco as they will push you to your best.
Cons: There is some cons to mention however. Again and again, I keep seeing people who are toxic to the organisation promoted. Positive encouragement and a flexible culture should be fostered and those that promote this culture of pushing boundaries, thinking outside the box, creativity, and making decisions with a bit of gut should be moved forward. Those who hold a traditional view of the office, making every i is dotted and every t is crossed, with their archaic ways and no value add to the company should be kept in positions where they have no influence over the culture or better, removed.

Cons: Politics with a capital P plus some; Innovation is a prized quality at Cisco however individuals trying to work through and contribute to transformation are passively punished for not doing things "the Cisco way"; Lack of alignment between enterprise strategy and team executions - most managers keep doing what they want to do regardless of what the stated organization and corporate strategy; Frequent and disruptive leadership shakeups in IT; non-engineering roles - despite lip service are not valued; There is very little respect for work-life balance unless you put your own boundaries up - which is problematic especially as we strive to do better with mental health for ourselves and our co-workers. A lot of managers and directors here take as much as is offered without consideration to how much they should take and then perversely shame you for overworking yourself.

Pros:
Cisco is a great place to work for many reasons:

1. As an employee, you are considered a valuable resource.  John Chambers, our CEO, often refers to us as the "Cisco Family", and the company tries to treat everyone like they are a family member.

2. Flexible work environment: I often telecommute several times a week.  I really only have to come in when I have collaborative face-to-face meetings with other engineers.  As long as I'm being productive and adding to the team, I've never been hassled for working from home.

3. Cisco benefits are competitive.  Not only do they offer the major financial benefits, but they also pay for my cell phone, home phone, & internet connection.  I also have been given lots of opportunities to try out products in my home.

4. Great work/life balance.  I insist on working only 40 hours/wk and not checking my email on the weekends.  I've gone 3 years with no complaints on that.  I often duck out of work early or come in late for doctors appts or other family affairs.  My manager and Cisco as a whole is very insistent that you do what's best for you and your family first.
Cons:
If you are uncomfortable with change, Cisco might not be the place for you.  There are significant leadership and strategy changes as we adapt to different markets.  Many projects we work on are started and stopped haphazardly by product marketing or senior leadership.  

Cisco often competes against itself, which can be frustrating at times.  This is why you probably shouldn't get too attached to one product or technology, cause you probably won't be working on it for long.  You will often walk a fine line between quality and time-to-market.

Pros: Flexible time and there is no permission needed if you want to work from home sometimes on an ad hoc time. All you need to do is send an email to your group in the morning that you are "WFH" (working from home) and how you can be contacted. There are so many resources available for professional development. There is support for mentoring programs. The work is challenging and fun. Individual work goals are decided based on department goals, which are in turn decided based on goals trickling down from the topmost level. The management is great and there is no micro-management. The people are great to work with. Really, what else does one want in an employer? Oh yeah... the benefits and compensation are among the best in the industry.
Cons: Really, I cannot think of much that is wrong with Cisco. My manager could be somewhat more appreciative of a job well done, and also have some more 1-1 time; but you cannot draw any conclusions from that because my previous manager - the only other manager that I have had at Cisco - was superb at keeping the communication lines open. I never wondered about what he thinks of me & my work because he would give feedback, positive or negative, on such a continuous basis. Another thing is that Cisco does not throw as many lavish parties or have celebrations like AOL (my previous employer) did, but I would rather have my employer be frugal, make profits and keep me employed than make losses due to extravagance and have to lay me off, which is what AOL had to do.

Pros:

I enjoy working here and consider it my best experience to date.  Having done various roles within Cisco and worked in different functions, I can say that you truly have an opportunity to grow and advance your career; destiny is in your hands if you can produce.
Cons:
If you just treat Cisco as a job, then this isn't a great place for you as they don't pay well, their compensation isn't up to speed and you work your tail off with little to no recognition.  Supreme results are just the "ticket to the dance" and to truly thrive you need to put in 150% in order to stand out from the rest of the crowd.

Working in a large company has its pros and cons, and with 65000 people, its only going to get more spread out, thin and as we expand into new markets and technologies, we need to trust the the people we hire are pushing just as hard as we are.  

I'm not sure people are coasting, but there are people in Cisco who seem to have their jobs because they were in the right place at the right time.  I wouldn't mind seeing some of the old guard go so we can step up and have our chance in the spotlight.  But this is few and far in between; we just have to wait our turn.

It has a big company feel and things happen at a much slower pace.  I hear we're becoming process-heavy and this has caused complaints within the ranks.  I would like to see us turn on a dime much faster, put out releases at a faster pace still balance that with quality.  

I've had a chances to interact with the CEO on down and some people are extremely arrogant (as I am, so why am I complaining), but this is what you get when you hire the best of the best.

There are certain "good jobs" that everyone seems to want and they're extremely hard to get.  You have to be resourceful and think out of the box in order to land one.

Pros:
Wow! It really looks like the recent layoffs and expense reduction measures at Cisco have brought out the discontented lot. Unfortunately, that seems true of many comments left on blogs or user review sites, where the majority of posts often serve as an outlet for those who aren't happy.  I have been guilty of that as well, only posting a review when I was really disappointed, rather than when I had an Ok experience. 

I'm not an old timer..I have been with Cisco for the past 5 years and lucky to have a good manager . Yes, things in the last two years have gone downhill in terms of cutbacks. Even in Sales, all non-customer travel was cut. As late as 2007, you could just book a flight and travel without manager authorization. None of that was going to survive the recession and unfortunately neither did the free sodas. The layoffs( or re-structuring as management would like to call them because they were less than 5% of the employee base) didn't help either.  

Having said that, at least from my perspective Cisco still has quite a few redeeming qualities.All the negative reviews don't explain how Cisco was in Fortune's Top 10 best companies to work for last year and is still at number 16 this year - after all the cuts. So, my comparison point might be different, but I think its not just the above average compensation package that includes generous 401(K) matches,annual bonuses, option grants given annually (unfortunately,those are history - the last one I got was in 2007 and they are very much under water). It's also the quality of people one interacts with (and yes, some of them were managers), the tremendous number of opportunities to move internally and take on new assignments. Also, for sales professionals especially, Cisco's market leadership usually translates to exposure to premium accounts and high commissions. 

There's a big emphasis on work-life balance and its best exemplified by the 4 weeks of vacation that is standard for all employees...that is a very rare thing. Webex meetings are the norm for most internal meetings, so there's great flexibility when it comes to working from home or any other location. There's also a strong culture of giving back that I found very commendable. Volunteering is highly encouraged and Cisco matches all individual charitable contributions up to a $1000 per year. This doesn't include their annual holiday fund-raising effort where all contributions are effectively tripled.
Cons:
Like most big companies, Cisco has its share of problems. John Chambers has created a very Sales centric culture based on M&A, rather than focusing on engineering innovation. Loyalty is punished when spin-offs are re-acquired for high valuations. Overall, if you have pre-2000 stock options or are in Sales, life is good, but I'm not sure I can say the same thing for IT or Engineering. The culture there tends to be very bureaucratic with a fair number of folks who are only interested in maintaining status quo.  In the IT groups, there's an undue emphasis on costs and much of the work has been outsourced which turns out to be quite unproductive. My interaction with Sales IT left much to be desired and even friends working there want to move out of those groups. Just as engineers in the Business units hope that an evening MBA will free them from the confines of the engineering organization. 

Cisco's stock pool being very diluted, there's not much upside when it comes to appreciation. Career growth and chances of promotion depends to a large extent on how much support you get from your manager and how many of his/her peers you influence, so you really have to manage upwards, besides doing the best job you can and then hope that its enough.

Pros: Opportunity to learn and carve out your own path of expertise, but that changed a couple of years ago.
Cons: Politics have gotten out of control, good people are no longer recognized for their good work, its all about perception and visibility even if you get nothing of substance that impacts the business done.

Pros: Good work/life balance. Bonuses were reasonably good until this year.
Cons: When on the same week the company announces a layoff of 5000 employees, you also have the CEO reporting record compensation for himself, it tends to affect motivation within. Cisco has a tendency of putting or promoting under-qualified individuals in key roles. At this point I feel the company is in an irreversible  downward spiral. Many executives are jumping ship in the face of Software Defined Networking and the disruption it represents to Cisco's fat margins on its core product line.

Pros: Room to grow, working with bright minds and cutting edge technology.
Cons: There are challenges as the company is in a restructuring mode ever year, people are afraid to lose their job even if they are performing.

Pros: Flexible Schedule.   Depending on your group, they allow you to work from home 2 days a week.    There are still lots of really good and really smart people around.
Cons: Cisco is currently going through another round of restructuring and layoffs.   This seems to be a perennial event.   The reason for laying off is not always clear.   It looks like they are consolidating hardware and moving more into a software model. They are making big cuts in technical documentation in the US and moving everything offshore.

Pros: Cisco is a great company going through a lot of a changes to expand into new businesses.  There are a lot of talented and passionate people, and a really great place for new university grads, especially with software experience.  The compensation/benefits are really good.  There are long days especially if you work with people in other timezones but there is flexibility in your schedule.
Cons: In some groups, the jobs are being moved to lower cost locations outside of San Jose, and there are also a lot of contract positions.

Pros: Its a great place to learn if you are starting your career. Lots of freedom and no micro management
Cons: if you are a red badge they treat you like  bad/ s.h.i.t .. Dont trust anyone even your closest friend in the job because they can stab you back. I dont recommend to work here if you have a family that depends on you anything can happen

Pros: Great pay, great benefits, great bonus.  Collaborative environment.  Top notch talent.  Challenging work.  No day ever the same.  Networking leader.
Cons: Long hours, layoffs every fall.  Last several years has seen the same restructuring and RIFs every fall.  Many people in constant fear for their jobs.

Pros: Excellent benefits that allow for flexibility. Working remotely is supported and made possible by our amazing collaboration technology (WebEx, TelePresence, Jabber, and more). You're encouraged to innovate in your job and try something new if it will benefit a program. People are very open and friendly to newcomers. I've found that people are generally willing to share their career journeys and lessons learned. Plenty of internal development opportunities (stretch assignments, rotations, internal reqs, etc).
Cons: It's a big company, so it takes a while to know who to contact to get things done quickly.

Pros: Very competent and friendly people.  Everyone very cooperative and willing to help you get acclimated, learn the various tools and systems, etc.  Lot of opportunities to volunteer in company-sponsored community service activities.  Large company, lots of opportunity to move to different jobs and acquire new experience.
Cons: For contractors (at least in the department where I worked) not enough formal newcomer training and orientation to help you get up to speed quickly.  Needed a lot of help from co-workers which inconvenienced them (although all were very understanding and helpful.)

Pros: The senior management is easy to approach. They are ready to help whenever necessary. Lots of work. Snacks are available and during releases, dinner too.
Cons: The work is slow paced for an entry level employee. If you are assigned to something, it is difficult to shift your focus to something else that you may be interested in.

Pros: Benefits are top-notch ; good 401K match; great Employee Stock purchase plan; great health benefits overall; salaries are very good; flexible work hours
Cons: culture has changed over the years in not a favorable direction as seen by many; career development is not consistent and a bit undervalued

Pros: Salaries are high for Ottawa.
Cons: Command and control is awful. They have an elitist technical leadership system, where who you are is way more important than how good your idea/knowledge is. All technical decisions are centralized with the elite, who reside in San Jose.

Pros: Good benefits, nice gyms, good cafes, has ESPP, Work From Home options (depending on group). Lots of runway to get projects off the ground, if management wouldn't ground the projects.
Cons: Too big of a company to get out of their own way. Management hithers the process and does not help grow the company or individual engineers. To further the issue, there were no checks and balances between what VPs were asking and what management was telling you to do. Micro management could be a real issue.

Pros: This is a very good company to work for with many benefits, especially the ability to work from home.  Many opportunities to learn and grow, and rotate in potential roles, if interested.
Cons: No life/work balance, work long hours, especially with global teams in various time zones.  Cisco is changing at a rapid pace in order to to stay relevant with their competitors.  Expectations from management may be high as a result.

Pros: Good Company to work for with some talented people.  Flexible re work live balance
Cons: Limited promotion possibilities.  Long term management are favoured and they look after each other.  The yearly cuts in the workforce is stressful, as you just don't know if you'll have a job come the new fiscal. You basically have a job with Cisco for year at a time.

Pros: A great company that has provided me many opportunities over the last nearly 20 years.
Cons: Transitioning from a hardware business to an annuity-based software model is hard.  There are too many people who aren't ready/willing to make that transition and are stuck in the past.

Pros: Virtual set-up is excellent (you pay for your ISP access and cell phone). Training is widely available in your chosen discipline. Excellent for remote workers, but watch your "6" all the time.
Cons: When it come to reorgs, layoffs do not offer employees rehoming opportunities. You have to apply to listed positions. During a layoff period, people applying are viewed differently. Cisco relies HEAVILY on contractors (contracts are 90 days w/extensions) and H-1Bs.

Pros:
- Flexible work / Work life balance
- Autonomy 
- Innovation 
- Smart and talented people
- If you own your career, we can easily move internally
Cons:
- Being a big company, there are a lot of processes on a daily basis to cope with
- Lay offs followed by recruitment phase
- International move more complex

Pros:
Excellent compensation and work conditions
Very good options for internal education
Seem to be committed to good social values, like non-discrimination per color, creed, etc.
Cons:
Big-company bureaucracy
Lots of blah-blah from upper management... buzzwords rather than clarity. There seems to be a culture built around this, leading to unclear lines of responsibility and obscure job titles
Atmosphere of uncertainty about continuing employment; the threat of the next layoff is always hanging overhead, lowering motivation among the real workers
Possible age-related discrimination in layoffs

Pros: Remote work, opportunity to do work you enjoy, work-life balance, competitive salary, great benefits, 100% matching 401(k)
Cons: Talent mobility is non-existent, fear of  yearly layoffs-work slows from June to Oct because of this uncertainty, longer you are there the higher chances you will get laid off, replacing older workers and hiring younger with no business sense, poor leadership in some areas of business-no effective strategy to identify, retain and promote "good" leaders

Pros: Lots of work, good tech to be involved in. Clients appreciative and value work. Cutting edge solutions and support are just that... cutting edge without precedence.
Cons: Although periodically expressed otherwise, in the real time application upper senior and executive teams are dis-jointed to the staff that actually work with clients face to face daily.

Pros:
It is a great introduction to Cisco, with good opportunities to learn a lot. It is divided into three categories of learnings within sales acumen, professional and technical skills. 
Cisco invests heavy in the candidates and does not expect a short-term return on investment, so you will experience a really thorough program. 
There is great international opportunities and it is very easy to create a great network.
Cons: Before you start to get commission, the wages are not that high.

Pros: Flexible work environment, collaborative, growth potential
Cons: None to discuss at this time

Pros: Everything. The trust the flexibility the perks. I might be lucky with the management I have, but I hear so many people with the same kind of good luck.
Cons: Can't figure out anything I don't like. Maybe w could have free drinks or free food. Everything else is just perfect.

Pros: Work flexibility, and  good compensation.
Cons: Oldschool management and thinking. Very corporate. Bureaucratic. People are in the wrong role and cannot do their job. Recruiting processes are sloppy, we are not recruiting the right people and for the right jobs well enough and this is a burden on the teams because we don't know how to fire them.

Pros: Development, benefits, overall programs, personal and professional advancement, good technology.
Cons: A big company can suffer some bad managers.  Changes too often to be stable in marketplace, be prepared for change.  Pays lip service to programs and often only succeeds because of 1 or 2 dedicated individuals.  If those individuals go, then the programs often go too.

Pros:
-Free access to udemy,pluralsight and lynda portals(learning)
-Breakout areas
-Paternity/maternity benefits
-Bereavement leave
-Transport facilities(free if part of 24*7 support)
-Good food/free if part of 24*7 team
-Redeemable certification costs,subject to department (Cisco certs can be redeemed in most cases)
Cons:
-Not easy to move across departments/roles
-Usual office preferential treatments/politics

Pros: Working at Cisco becomes like being in a very large family. There is a tremendous understanding that your coworkers are watching out for you, willing to help at a moment's notice, and truly care about your success. I worked here for over 20 years, and had a very difficult time choosing to leave.
Cons: The pay is very good, but lagging some of the competition.

Pros: Cisco lives its values. It's high empathy, conscious culture has made it one of the best places I have ever worked. It tends to encourage employees to focus on their strengths vs weaknesses.
Cons: It is a very large organization and at the same time, often a consensus-driven culture. As such, it takes skill, energy and more time than in smaller companies to drive alignment and change.

Pros: Good compensation, good work life balance
Cons: The promotion system encourages people speak more than work.

Pros: The people and the ability to work in a hybrid manner with excellent technology! Appreciate the outspoken support from Leadership on Social Justice issues and community support.
Cons: Not the most progressive in cascading Diversity & Inclusion changes throughout the organization. The ELT leads in this area but not felt as strongly throughout the company, and it shows when you look at our numbers.

Pros: Cisco was a place where we worked hard and we treated each other with respect. I was fortunate to have great managers throughout my 20 years at Cisco. My managers gave me authority to make decisions and did not micromanage. I led a small team of software engineers and we had a great team chemistry.
Cons: The only downside was the sometimes unrealistic expectations of our customers. I was in software support and the customers expected instant results even on complex problems that took weeks to resolve.

Pros: The sheer diversity in terms of technology exposure, and the best Networking industry talent you can have as your colleagues. If you're interested in Routing, the Flagship Silicon one product line which is making waves in the industry is your go-to place. If you're into Switching , Cat9k, the highest selling switch on the planet is the team you want to be. Needless to say how cool Meraki is, and if you're into collab, you have multiple options and more.
Cons: Nothing major I can think of

Pros:
great team atmosphere 
good pay
good benefits
Cons: vaccine mandates in the US

Pros:
* Good work/life balance
* This depends on your team, but most people here are helpful and easy to work with
Cons:
* Lots of redundancy can at times lead to no accountability. 
* Engineers who are enthusiastic end up doing most of the work, but it doesn't always translate to proper recognition due to upper management not being technical. Connections and speaking in meetings are valued over actual work. 
* Things get done really slowly, and is often reactive and hardly proactive.

Pros: Worked with very intelligent developers and tech specialists. Exposure to high performance software engineering and advanced system architectures. Great experience for a tech career. Teams are effective at remote work.
Cons: Culture was weird, but maybe not too weird for a tech company. Some managers lacked training and support to contribute effectively. Senior management allowed a hostile, bullying culture among management, which definitely affected morale. Very resistant to promoting people from within, but quick to hire from outside, even when those hires lacked relevant experience.

Pros:
Work/life balance
Culture
Flexibility
ERGs
Once you find your support circle, they are great to lean on and leverage for career advice.
Cons:
Pay: sine this is was my first job post college I didn't really know my worth. I didn't negotiate my salary, which has plagued me throughout my career. 
Management opportunities: I have been overlooked far too often for management opportunities that I am more than qualified to do. Although the company claims DEI is important, too many leaders of colors have left and I don't see the investment in rising minority leaders.

Pros: freedom to work the hours at home or at the office, no one pays attention to where you are just as long as you are on one of the many conf calls then tend to substitue for work.  In an average day most people spend more then half their time listening in on calls.
Cons: management is more concerned with process then actual results, fictious cost savings are considered accomplishments, hours spent on cals are considered productivity

Pros: Big company. Have more chances to move to other groups when you want to challenge yourself. Nice buildings and onsite landscape.
Cons: Used to give out more benefits. No more free soda and free stuff. Food price in cafeteria increased a lot and the quality with quantity also reduced!

Pros:
Opportunities within the company
High salary
Women are treated equally
Liberal work-at-home policy
Excellent benefits
Cons:
Long hours
Inept mddle management
Lack of opportunities within one's department
Fear of having your job sent overseas
Older workers are encouraged to leave with early retirement, taking their skills and expertise with them. Management needs to be assessed and culled.

Pros: Competitive pay for new hires, good brand recognition, excellent campus, good transport system, women friendly (good wfh options)
Cons: No culture of excellence. India development is mostly maintenance. For senior folks India is empire building, huge teams chugging out mindless work. Long term employees poorly rewarded. Losing out to competitors. Expats significantly adding to the cost with no tangible value add.

Pros: Work culture is good - there's a good sense of trust and delegation. Managers strive for work/life balance. In addition, there's a lot of diversity of job functions and roles.
Cons: For those coming from smaller companies or companies with less virtual meetings, adapting to the semi-virtual work environment takes time. Even if someone works at HQ, they might spend 70% of their time with virtual teams. Promotions take longer than at many other companies.

Pros: Great people and technologies.  Interesting things to work on.  Working remotely is the norm.  Competitive pay.  Decent benefits.  Stable job even as the markets and work changes.
Cons: No real clear paths for advancement.  HR isn't that good.  Low performers and bad managers take a long time to weed out.  Performance reviews are really just lip service to career development.  Communications from top-down aren't always clear.

Pros:
Compensation and bonus plan have been excellent
Ability to make moves to create a career (historically)
Work flexibility
Get to work with a lot of talented colleagues
Cons:
The Cisco "family" is really a myth and the culture has gone downhill
Four major reductions in force over the past five years
Cisco is starting to look and feel more like HP
Extraordinary political environment

Pros: Networking with People, Development opportunities, Good benefits, Flexible, encourage education & training
Cons: Bureaucratic & Highly political environment, lot of repetitive / competitive work in parallel groups, lack of consistent messaging on strategy, Focus on individual LOB rather than whats good for the company

Pros: Great company, people with broad reach and opportunity across market. Very respected company within marketplace.
Cons: Tend to get overwhelmed with internal process' that takes you away from the customer far to often. Challenging for continued double digit growth especially within mature markets, given enterprise market attitude and improving acceptance of cloud based solutions and offerings.

Pros: Very intelligent people work in the DCSTG, there's a lot to learn from working with them.
Cons: Employee body is not very diverse, I found it more difficult to find friends than I have elsewhere. Workplace isn't especially exciting or interesting. Cubes have high walls, muted colors and hospital lights. Compensation isn't as good for comparable positions elsewhere.

Pros: Fantastic place to be "in the thick" of the technology landscape. Respected name in the industry makes it easy to get appointments with prospects (in sales) and the respect of technology professionals. Great place to learn.
Cons: Starting to grow to the point of being unwieldy (think IBM). Direct management has very little oversight and can limit exposure to upper-management, creating an environment where one person can determine the fate of your career not only in their organization but throughout the company.

Pros: Really bright people.  Collaboration is the culture with advanced technology to do it.  Terrific benefits.  Lots of training available.  Amazing amount of online content any time.  Flexible schedules and work from home setups.
Cons: Bureaucracy can slow things down.  Collaboration is good, but some times too many cooks in the kitchen.

Pros: Great team, lots of talented people. Never had a better experience with such knowledgeable and approachable co-workers. Big company with lots of resources. Great benefits and time-off. Good work/life balance.
Cons: Upper management makes arbitrary changes in organization and goals that rarely improve the business and often frustrate or efforts. Very little internal R & D. Prefer to acquire or spin-out then spin-in new ideas. Office facilities are out of date, grungy carpets and cubicles.

Pros: Global reach of the organization provides the opportunity to work with a diverse group of bright people.   Innovative, Fun place to work.  Interesting products and services
Cons: constant churn, reorganization, lay-off's and shifting priorities tend to bring down employee morale and result in hours of re-work picking up the work load of employees no longer with the company.

Pros: There's a freedom to act like an entrepreneur to get things done - Cisco has some great assets and some great people - and if you can pull these together, you can get great things done.
Cons: The company is large - serving Governments, Enterprises, Telcos, Webcos and SMB businesses - and this creates complexity in both Engineering and Delivery that can slow the business.

Pros: Company has a lot of opportunities for growth and allows a lot of flexibility in terms of hours you work and environment you work in. Many people tend to work from home including myself
Cons: Company culture has shifted. Where it was good to collaborate with other teams an drive cross organization efficiency it has become very political. Many of teams are trying to build empires or hold other teams responsible to pay for things. Company doesn't value experience as much as it used too.

Pros: Great and super flexible work environment.  For the most part you can work from home whenever you feel like it.  Challenging work. Descent Salary.
Cons: Company is too big.  Upper management doesn't seem to know what is going on at the bottom.  The structure and groups are constantly changing.  Too many products.  Engineering is dominated by a mafia.

Pros: great company culture, great products, great people, great compensation and benefit package, fast pacing high demanding company. #1 Champion League Player.
Cons: got over time too big, too many layer, some people do politics vs delivering on company mission and interest, you need to belong to the inner circle to progress career.

Job Title: Gm & senior director, cloud video & software solution sales
Pros: Good pay and inspirational new CEO. Work from home policy is good. Too big to fail, as in nobody else has e2e portfolio plus war chest to fill major gaps
Cons: High job insecurity. Lay offs every quarter. Short term focus always. Passive aggressive US sales culture. Major internal focus as a consequence of historically being a Partner led sales structure

Pros: Most people you'll work with are impressive, professional, and approachable.  The company is so large that it's easy to move around - as long as you know someone.  Having the flexibility to work from home when needed is terrific.
Cons: Annual layoffs at the beginning of the fiscal year are now an accepted part of the culture.  The only time the email stops is during the shut down in late Dec.  Leadership ranges from great in some organizations to virtually non-existent in others.

Pros: Great name to have on your CV. Very much empowered on the day to day. Good internal systems.   Interesting thoughts but drinking the cisco 'cool aid' leads to poor understanding of the market
Cons: Terrible middle management. Lots of jobs for the clique. Culture was very much summed up in one phrase but a colleague 'cisco used to be a great place to work..now its just a place to work'

Pros:
I worked in the Bangalore office.
- Great Campus and a lot of activities/extra-curricular that one can involve in
- good cafeteria, gym, TT, air hockey, massage chair and what not! :D
Cons: I worked in one of the teams under NOSTG (Network Operating System Group). I had joined as a fresher. The work was boring as hell. It was a 15 year old legacy product and the work involved bug fixing and responding to customer issues. No development work as such. Would never recommend a fresher to join the company.

Pros:
The company is more open to teleworking than most.
The products are solid and the technology is interesting.
Benefits are competitive.
Cons:
Career opportunities are limited.  If you don't live near a corporate office, you'll be limited.
If you are an account manager, you can become CEO. If you are an engineer, you'll always be an engineer. Very few are allowed to escape the title.

Pros: Great people, smart, fun to work with.
Cons: Company is getting too top heavy with managers who only care how they look to other managers. Company hasn't learned how to communicate well, other than meetings, so there are too many of them.

Pros: Organized commute to work leading people to work 9 to 18, friendly for flexible time arrangements (for example for working mothers), involvement in Agile methodologies, lot of great and interesting people, experiments with new technologies, good pay for Jerusalem area.
Cons: Local management is overruled by central management decisions, no commitment to keep local development in tact, periodic downsizing strokes, low pay comparable to Tel Aviv area.

Pros: Best people in the business.  Great customer focused culture. Open door policy that really works.
Cons: HR and Finance have WAY too much power in the company.  Has become increasingly "PC" obsessed and risk averse.

Pros:
many different business units - so lots of opportunity to learn 
mix of good and bad organizations: do your homework before joining.  Each business unit has its own culture

Overall good company to spend a couple of years in and then leave.
Cons:
-low pay, not much advancement
-lots of nepotism.  I worked in ~ 5 business units and each of them were stacked with their own 'in' crowd
-lack of innovation

Pros: Individuals are great, benefits are pretty good, especially parental leave, and work/life seems fine.
Cons:
Company messaging is contradictory with company action at times.  Particularly when it comes to their agile transformation.
And yearly layoffs are stressful, and seem to happen to just about anyone.

Pros:
Stability- company is a leader amongst its competition. 
Lot of teams to chose from to move internally
Flexible Work hours
Good packages for lateral hires
Cons:
Good work generally goes unrecognized - unless you make efforts to promote yourself.
Hikes and promotions are far and few. Layoffs generally happen during hike/appraisal period - may be this is deliberately done.
Frequent org level changes - keeps one guessing if their team will be fired.

Pros: The company is on track turning into more software income.  CEO Chuck is doing a good job and the overall strategy works for the company.
Cons: Some regions are undergoing restructure of the organization and the politics were horrible.  Not a good place if the goal is finding a fun place.  This is the company asks for results and thus everything is results oriented.

Pros: Good PTO (4 weeks per year) and bonus program.  Flexible working hours and work from home is common.  The company is growing again after several years revenue decline. The transition to software and subscription business pays off. Very good learning place for folks who just start their career as the company has good process and infrastructure.
Cons: Multiple rounds of layoff/restructuring when revenue is down. Selective downsizing in certain business still takes place so that resource will be invested in new growth area. So it depends on the team you are in.

Pros: Working with very smart, happy and motivated people; Interested in your personal growth; Strategy and GTM supports where the industry is headed; excellent opportunities for women; Provide excellent forums to keep all employees current on business priorities and company initiatives; Values "giving back" by matching donations and even giving "Paid Time Off" to serve.
Cons: Working with such smart, motivated people can also be a little intimidating;  Bigger companies take a little longer to get things done (no  different than other big companies)

Pros: Some really great people you get to work with on projects.  Reasonable pay and benefits.  Peers within and outside of Canada are some of the smartest and wonderful people I had the pleasure of working with.
Cons: Constant reorgs. No real strategy. No such thing as work life balance. Perpetual layoffs. Culture of nepotism, classicism etc. in the Toronto office.  Positions to advance career not based on merit but who is in the "cool kids" circle and who is not.

Pros:
- Very flexible working hours
- Competitive salary
- One of the greatest Health Insurance Package
- WFH when needed
- Free EV charger in parking lot

Not sure about other teams but my manager values my work and I receive a lot of bonus end of the year.
Cons:
- Ottawa office has a terrible cafeteria, have to bring your own lunch
- QA teams are mostly in India and communication about the defects they submit gets very tricky due to time zone difference.

Pros: Inclusive and diverse environment, friendly and brilliant people, opportunity to grow. These are the first advantages that first come up to me when I think about this company. At Cisco you can be yourself and be awarded for that. Also, you will always find someone willing to help you. The best workplace in the world is that place where you find the motivation to work hard and you are pushed to be the best version of yourself everyday. This place for me is Cisco.
Cons: No disadvantages so far for me.

Pros: I've really enjoyed my time at Cisco. While it is a very large company, with all the associated problems that can bring, if you find yourself in a great team surrounded by fantastic people (like I did), you will have an awesome time at Cisco.
Cons: There is a huge amount of organisational issues that can make it hard to make an impact, but if you have the gumption and are willing to fight the machine, you can get a lot done!

Pros: Strong top company leadership team
Cons: Still very much dominated by male leadership in product development and engineering. Lots of talk of making a change, but it didn't happened in my many, many years I spent there. The top leadership of the company talks about diversity, equality, and no bullying, but it doesn't make it down the chain.

Pros: Cisco is a mature company with a lot of benefits/perks for employees such as on campus gyms, subsidized dining, ESPP, and on site healthcare. The sales teams are generally collaborative and work/life balance is pretty good. Easier to predict business than other companies.
Cons: Not a place to go if you want agility and speed. Very layered and bureaucratic compared to newer companies.

Pros:
- Allows for remote working with financial support to buy WFH equipment.
- Regular company "check-ins" from management to employees so we always know what's going on. 
- Company wide 5 free "time-to-give" days to the charity of your choice.
Cons: -Pay bands not clear for the different job grades. i.e. you can find a grade 8 earning more than a grade 10.

Pros: There is very open communication between employees on projects, and vast learning resources are available. Employees are very focused on providing solutions for customer issues.
Cons: The firm is becoming bureaucratic management wise. It takes a long time to make decisions on major product directions. After many acquisitions, the organization is top-heavy, which leaves little room for internal promotion into the higher management ranks.

Pros: I came back to Cisco after 11 years.  It's great to have on your resume and I'm always very proud to say I work there.  They truly believe in a balanced life.
Cons: Hiring Pause...sometimes they lose really GREAT employees because they cannot convert a contractor to a regular employee.   While contributing as a contractor, your ideas aren't as widely embraced due to your status.

Pros: Lot of exposure to different technologies, so much to learn about networks. Good people. Good HR.
Cons:
Bad management, no work life balance. No risk taking in spite of stable company. They have hired donkeys to manage stallions :P
There is no cool culture of a start-up.

Pros:
Friendly workplace with people genuinely interested in helping each other and listening to the customers' needs. Open door policy and very frugal culture. 
Work life balance is possible when working on a stable mature business unit.
Good place if you want to understand how to sell in big scale, sales workforce is impressive. Opportunities to learn some industry trends and hear customers opinions if connected with the right Marketing persons.
Cons:
Very limited career development opportunities. Cisco now emphasizes a policy of career mobility, meaning that you are encouraged to look for opportunities within the company as a mean to compensate for lack of growth. Management now uses this policy to avoid any meaningful discussions under  the excuse that if you don't like something in your job then you are free to find something elsewhere (instead of addressing the job concerns).

Promotions are driven by the revenue importance of the product you work on. If you work on a non-established, emerging product then forget about advancing your career (Senior management will use those emerging projects in their favor to get visibility and pitch innovations though). 

In certain units, the job recognition is severely distorted: with management and teams raising a problem, later solving it,  then becoming the hero for resolving something that they must have avoided in the first place with proper thinking. Many managers have become masters at playing this game and Sr. mgmt plays along. On the other hand, teams who silently consistently execute well, may not get any visibility or recognition.

The company is no longer what it used to be 10 years ago. It has become a mature workplace with internal politics and limited employee growth. Great place to start a career and then go to a startup or another company genuinely interested in product innovations with true meritocracy.

Pros: If you just want to work for sake of working and consistent pay checks then Cisco is the place for you. If you are sincere, hardworking and ambitious (Want return for your hard work) then Cisco bureaucracy will kill you. You will be defeated again and again.
Cons: Lots of politics. Management just want to use employees to earn hefty returns. There are so many useless management positions.

Pros: The Cisco culture was a great motivator.  The work is flexible, the financial rewards are good and most employees are driven and hard-workers.
Cons: Ever increasing red tape.  Culture is fading.  Too many layers of management and less accountability.  Progression within the company is not easy and not really structured.

Pros:
Some of the best reasons to work at Cisco are:
1. Cool technology
2. Work from anywhere
3. Pride in the company
4. Benefits package
5. Salary compensation
6. Work/life balance
Cons:
Some of the things I don't miss about working at Cisco:
1. You are never "off the clock"
2. Some of their processes became processes for the sake of process
3. Technology for technologies sake.

Pros: Good company, use of latest cutting-edge softwares and procedures, access to work from home, close to where I live, competitive compensation to employees and contractors.
Cons: Not the most "fun" place to work, as with many other companies there is a lot of politics in the company, long hours, unrealistic deadlines.

Pros:
The leadership is ethically sound, and an ethical culture is promoted. Employees are compensated fairly and managers are encouraged to be considerate towards allowing a good work/life balance.
Engineers get to work on modern and leading-edge network technologies, often with a deep worldwide market penetration, which can be rewarding.
Cons:
Cisco does not have any real research division. All work is very product-to-market focused.
The company is very big, which means bureaucratic processes, red tape and in-fighting.
Engineers work in very boring cubicles. The "break rooms" are noisy, dirty kitchens.

Pros: The benefits are very good, especially the medical, dental, and vision plans. Good budget for learning opportunities. Travelling to other parts of the world and working with colleagues. The culture is competitive, making you want to do your best.
Cons: Often work nights and weekends because you're always connected. Since 2001, they have yearly layoffs. The managers need to be trained better in order to motivate employees.

Pros: At Cisco, it is almost guaranteed that you will be working on a fun, relevant,and interesting project. There's never a shortage of things that need to get done. It is a fast-paced, competitive environment, but you are surrounded by many intelligent people who are willing to help. They offer very competitive salary and are great about coordinating extracurricular activities.
Cons: There are at times disconnects between the many managers and developers. Also, long hours are often necessary as you must always get your work done and abide by sometimes strict deadlines.

Pros: Lots of training on the best of breed products across the latest and greatest solutions the industry has to offer.
Cons: Sometimes you are forced to sell a solution that may be going end of sale but the information has not gone public. This can lead to loss of customer trust and result in more difficult sales in the future.

Pros:
Cisco has tremendous Brand strength and recognition
Cisco has great integrity with Employees, and with Customers
Excellent people here and there among a generally weak
Cons:
Leadership weaknesses at mid-level
Excellent people below Management-level paid below market, unless in Sales
Not much commitment to key employees at acquired companies
Some long-term Management has been promoted above their competence level

Pros: Opportunity (worked in Mfg, Eng, and Finance), highly-recognized brand, supportive of continued education (MS, MBA, etc.), dominant positions in most markets.
Cons: You really need to proactively manage your career here.  B/c this is a big company, you can get lost in the shuffle quite easily.  As a company, we are in the $40B/year range, so only time will tell if Cisco can bust through that barrier or fizzle.

Pros: Decent (but by no means lavish) benefits, some great smart people to work with.
Cons: Executives are out of touch with their employees, partners, and customers. It's a company that's not really growing, and the stock price reflects that. It depends on acquisitions for innovation. Layoffs are now an annual tradition, so for many people job "stability" is a myth--but you still have all the challenges of working at a huge company.

Pros:
1. Flexible hours, work from home option. 
2. Good bonus. 
3. Great benefits. Onsite medical facilities. Free shuttles to bart/caltrain/san francisco.. 
4. Challenging work and cutting edge technology in some teams. Quality of work and management varies widely across teams/business units.
Cons:
Big bloated company, too many layers of management. 
Not a fun workplace. Workplace Resources department is very inefficient and does a poor job.

Pros: Great collegues, good pay, nice working environment
Cons: Too many cuts in the workforce that do not align to the business direction. Too little support from the Executive level towards making the workforce feel needed. A lot of marketing and sales speak with no real results. Sometimes way to slow to react.

Pros: Team Environment, Technology Innovation, Competitive Salary and Benefits Package and a Win/Win Organizational Culture
Cons: Stock analyst's perception of the company and its leadership, aggressive acquisition strategy and the company has the best group of human capital out there but they must invest in retaining and enhancing that talent more in order to position themselves as the top technology innovator in the current era.

Pros: You get the opportunity (or are forced) to learn the technology. Ambitious people get what they want in this American culture.
Cons: Managers tend to think certificates are important and let evaluations depend on them. You are nothing but a pawn on a big checker board. The one who yells most, gets most. Some decisions taken by directors or managers are not all that logical and when they fail, they have very big umbrellas. Not much work-life balance. Work from home option is a covert for holiday for some.

Pros: Great benefits, from bonuses, stock, fitness centers, training, and more.  In addition there are plenty of opportunities to move different groups.
Cons: Being a big company, there is a lot of bureaucracy, which causes projects to move slow.  A lot of the tools and projects are antiquated.  A lot of the engineering resources are dedicated to maintenance rather than new projects.

Pros: Having the opportunity to work with smart intelligent people, who are equally as devoted to make the product better is a always a pleasure. Working in a DevOps culture, owning the product end to end and making sure its scalable and performant all come with challenges but good challenges to have.
Cons: None that I can think of, been here just over 3 years and enjoying everyday of my work still. Not many people can say that.

Pros: Decent benefit, intelligent workers, great IT support dept, PTO
Cons: Corporation get too big, some a lot of inter-office bureaucracy, lack transparency.  Some managers are more political animals than people manager, who are more interested in his/her personal gain, rather than the team growth.

Pros: Flexible work arrangements, smart people, good management
Cons: It's hard to get promoted to management in our group.  Our department often hires from outside our group (but still internal).  This is discouraging from our own team's perspective who work hard and achieve results to get to the next level.  I presume this approach occurs to bring in a fresh set of eyes as well as a means to leverage the relationships from the outside hire.

Pros: Great customers and partners around the world… legacy of 30 years of Cisco changing the world
Cons: passive aggressive internal politics, annual re-org and layoffs, lots of people have lots of ideas but complex org model makes it difficult to align and achieve corporate vision and strategy

Pros:
--Decent pay
--Remote work
--Good bonus, 401K plan, Health Insurance plans.
-- Work in latest technologies
Cons:

-- they juice the young chaps, project/program managers enjoy having work/life balance
--Not high quality PMs-  some PMs lack communication, negotiation and planning skills

Pros:

- Too many middle managers.
- Too many hoops to jump through to get anything done.

Pros: Good work environment. Professional . Nice people. Nice gym.  Nice buildings. Good security. Nice location.

Individual contributors get screwed when senior management makes terrible decisions on projects to pursue and project is a failure - no accountability at the VP and director levels.

Pros: Team is good and work environment is good. Good project to work on and highly motivated colleagues with good exposure to work.
Cons: Yearly layoffs and workforce reductions. Also constant change in upper management. Our group has had 4 VPs in less than a year.

Pros: The CEO just turned over, and the new CEO is showing signs of positive change, which are already showing throughout the organization.  A focus on cloud, a desire to for organizational agility.  Smart, aggressive people get rewarded.
Cons: Not everyone has gotten the memo that things are changing at Cisco.  It gets difficult to rally the entire organization, because the entire organization is so massive.

Pros: Not a lot to share- Cisco once was a great company but got lost in the 50+ market adjaceny concept and lost it's way.
Cons:
No transparency - but management always says they're transparent.

Always talking about culture- but there is none.  The People Deal is just a marketing term for millennials.

Pros: Great people and teams who have a strong tradition of doing right by the customer and a passion for winning.
Cons: Very large company with quite a bit of politics now part of the business environment. In leadership, too much focus on internal processes and not as enough time & focus on our Customers and Teams (the things that really matter)

Pros: Work from home, good benefits RSU golden handcuffs.  Has cutting edge products.  Minimal travel required.  However the cons far outweigh the pros.

ClubsI worked in a team they devalued women & targeted all the senior level folks in a recent LR.  

Double standard in place - if you at married man with kids but lousy at your job then Cisco will keep you. If you a female then you will be treated like dirt.

Pros:
+ Bangalore Campus and facilities
+ flexibility to work from home
+ Internal movement
+ good for lower grades and juniors
Cons:

- very little new work, lot of maintenance type work
- little learning
- frequent lay offs

Pros: Too many to name! The people, the technology, the desire to give back and make a positive difference to the world. The ability to work hard but with flexibility to integrate your life outside of work. The support of caring, talented people who aspire for us to win. Wouldn't be any where else if given a choice!
Cons: I think sometimes we need to be more honest with one another. Sometimes I think the business suffers because we are all so nice and genuinely care about each other!

Pros: Cisco is a company that takes care of its employees. I've seen Cisco HR go out of its way to make sure employees are being taken care of. In such a large company, there is still a bit of a family feel.
Cons: Continual transitions, re-orgs and ever changing management expectations leaves teams often caught on ever-shifting ground. It leads to missed expectations between employees and management, and a lot of stress, frustration and even fear as a result.

Pros: Strong company culture overall. Strong mobile working culture leading to a healthy work life balance. Generally very competent management in the UKI operation. Company benefits are excellent overall.
Cons:
Cisco is in a period of transition as it looks to remain relevant in todays market place. This means a lot of new acquisitions predominantly within the cloud compute space. This has led to a currently confusing and dynamically changing portfolio.
Career progression can be slow once you've reached a certain sales level within Cisco due to the corporate banding structure.

Pros: Good initial pay if you know how to negotiate, good bonus, supportive leadership team and you are able to self-direct your initiatives and work focus
Cons: Out-of-date promotion policy - less about your performance and more about how long you have been with the company or if you have visibility with all managers not just your direct. A lot of people try to avoid work, so talented hires gets overburdened quickly.

Pros: Great benefits, Cisco does really care about it's employees and it does have an impact on your day to day work.
Cons: The team is not the best. The skill level of employees varies greatly and sometimes you will find yourself having to work with poorly skilled people who are really just slowing you down or you'll feel like you are training them. This holds specially true if you come from a a top company in your professional field where you're used to working with the best.

Pros: Great environment/team, multiple ways to grow and move-up, open platform for giving ideas and opinions, side projects available if you want them but not required, upper management cares
Cons: typical "corporate BS," competing interests keep you from making a difference sometimes, graded by arbitrary numbers a lot, you're allowed to give your opinion and ideas but actions are often not taken on them, major pay gaps between virtual and high-tough

Pros:
Great team and skills
Family First mentality
Great benefits

Hire & Fire mentality - you can be blowing out your metrics but if you or your team no longer fit in the plan, you're gone. Other companies I have worked for will try and slot you elsewhere in the company.
Entrepreneurial approach tends to backfire - duplication of efforts between teams sets up competition rather than collaboration... ultimately someone loses (not necessarily because the winner is better - a lot of nepotism).

Pros: Work from home options. Competitive pay outside of the Bay Area. Stock dividend.
Cons: Low productivity workforce. HIGHLY political. Virtually no regard for employee satisfaction. +40 yr old works are targeted for layoffs each year.

Pros:
Have been working at Cisco Systems in Collaboration technology Group for more than 10+ years. Must admit that its a great place to work, got chance to work with some of the most talented folks, there is a great team spirit, great opportunities to learn and grow technically.  Focus towards Customer is truly awesome. 
All in all, great work life balance and an excellent work culture. 
Cisco rocks.

Cons: I seriously dont have any cons to write

Pros:

Pros: Top technology, great people, and great benefits.

Pros: supportive, great work life balance, a company with integrity and strong giving back culture, an inclusive place for everyone to be the best version of themselves , flexibility

Pros:

Pros:

Pros: There's a lot to learn, in terms of dealing with people and learning how processes work. It's a good company for someone who's starting out in their tech writing career. Pros: Brand, Legacy, Cash-rich, Monopoly, Young talent

Pros: salary, healthcare, benefits, access to training

Pros: Strong branding with high customer credibility.  Responsible organization that will address customer issues to satisfaction.

Pros: Cisco is a financially stable company and offers a breadth of areas in which you can work. I personally have worked in three countries with Cisco, and feel they remain in a good position for long term growth.

Pros:

Pros: Telecommuting, good salaries, and that's about it

Stock price  (saw it slide from over $30 to around $15 in the 2000s)

Pros: Good culture ,people trust you here.Good company to work with WFH option .

Pros: Life Oriented good balance between work and life. I had mostly positive experiences in my 13 year career. I would recommend this company highly for someone starting out in the corporate world.

Pros:

Pros: Competitive pay/benefits compared to similar industry/position. Leadership recognizes market movements and customer needs. Many great teams and subject experts to learn from. Many opportunities for lateral movement. If considering working here, judge on team basis, since quality of life/employees varies vastly between teams.
Cons: Management consists of politicians that would eat Obama for breakfast. Low employee diversity. Many stale/underperforming employees but cisco is very slow to fire (based on performance).

Pros: Telecommuting - almost everyone works from home at least a few days a week

Pros: stable job, good training program, good starting point, great layoff package.

not many exciting projects. a lot of bug fixing, and dirty work. ok salary. seldom promotion. 

some team works on very old technologies which are going to be out sourced to India. some team works on non-value-generating work. Like other major companies, playing politics is a must skill if you want to promote. Some good projects were killed by mis-management and politics.

Pros: Resources, people, work environment.  You can still find some people that care about the customer and will do what they can to help.

Older white guys being unfairly laid off because the company wants more diversity...who cares that the company owes at least a bit of it's success to the hard work of older white men.

Pros: Executive Visionary aptitude, overall virtual workforce, diversity, cash position, employee equity, adaptability to market transition, honesty!!

Pros: Entreprenurial (still a bit!), can do attitude, great people

Pros: Customers first. Cisco focuses a lot to provide customers a very flexible and complex suite of products. Love the people I work with. Job rotation and mobility allows employees to play different roles as part of their career progression

Pros: Good name with large market share. Lots of talented employees. Compensation used to be very good although not anymore since the bubble burst in 2001.

Pros: I spent the first few years of my career at Cisco.  I had friendly, well-educated co-workers who were happy to mentor me.  I also had a great work-life balance and learned a lot about professional software development.

Pros: Big company, good perks and that's where it stops.

Pros: Challenging work atmosphere, brand name, facilities such as gym, health care, 401k, work from home, flexible

Pros: Good benefits and supports involvement in community projects. Fast paced driving innovation with huge capability. After 20 years in IT and 6 months at Cisco, deffinately the right move. Still market leading.

Pros: Work life balance, Freedom to express and innovate, great perks and benefits

Pros: For the 17th year in a row, Cisco is among Fortune Magazine’s 100 Best Companies to Work For. Cisco is  IT leader and a  great multinational workplace full of highly skilled professionals. Pros: Good pay and ok benefits. The company was great at the beginning when I first joined over 16 years ago. Good moral and coworkers.

Pros: Flexible work-from-home policy. Reasonably good benefits.

Not to worry, they can just layoff staff and buy more with a technology that's currently hot.

Pros: Cisco TAC is a nice place to polish the technical skills, learn troubleshooting methodology, and get various kind of customer service experiences.

Pros: Cisco has adopted the Agile in a big way, its Campus is massive and state of the art and also the transport facility is excellent

Pros: great freedom to explore well-thought out new ideas

Pros: I worked at Cisco for over 6 years in a variety of roles and departments. The work life balance, especially the ability to work remotely, is arguably the best perk. The benefits are good, and I love the emphasis on giving back to the community.
Cons: Layoffs are large scale and happen on a regular cadence. This negatively impacts morale and your ability to get work done. Decisions take forever to make, and rarely stick. Cisco needs to define a better path forward and become a leader in something again!

Pros:
Empowerment at all levels 
Easy Access to management with no ego issues 
Automated processes
Focus on Value to Customer which has helped company do well over many business cycles.
Focus on innovation and owning its space.
Strong Ethics and giving back
Can Rotate and grow
Opportunities abound to keep learning and developing skills
Focus on doing rather than bragging
Can build long term career
Cons: While there is no overnight upside like pre-ipo companies but if you are looking to build long term career than the financial rewards would be fully satisfying, attractive and best.

Pros: Great salary, great benefits, great location, great opportunities

Pros: This is a company that knows where it's going and how to get there. It can turn on a dime and change direction with great agility.

Pros: Big company, lots of benefits.
Cons: The culture is struggling to evolve, but the old culture has a stronghold - too engineering driven, too reactive, not proactive, in approach to software design. Many silos inside product teams and company wide that poorly communicate and point fingers. Lots of churn, lots of duplicate work ... unfortunate with so much potential.

Pros:
- Flexible time
- Competitive salary
- Great colture of collaboration

In general, I strongly believe this is a very good working environment where I am surrended with happy people that show passion and dedication to their work.
Cons: None for now. I believe that if you are enthusiastic about your work, is going to be fine :)

Pros: Work Life Balance, Cisco gives time off for community service, Nice Co-workers
Cons: Constant layoffs, make sure to negotiate a high salary because you will never get a raise-- having a job is a considered your raise. There is not much diversity in certain teams -- seems some teams are made of the same ethnic group.

Pros:
Excellent benefits - better than any I have seen - period.
Brand Name
Opportunity to move between roles (provided manager is supportive)
Flexible work hours

Extremely low glass ceiling for India
Low Internal Hikes
Low chances of promotion
Growth dependent on purely manager's discretion as no formal review cycle

Pros: A decent Job with good benefits.

I wounder if Great Places to Work and Fortune Magazine interviewed any of the people forced to retire early or that got laid-off before giving Cisco 1# place to work again?

Pros:
1) Solid financial stability and wealth of IP, probably going to be here for next 25 years
2) Good work-life balance with decent pay
3) Goes above and beyond to support Employees in case of emergencies like health issues etc. + Giving back

1) Internal Innovation lacking, acquisitions don't work, too much competition internally (duplicate products or trying trying to compete with its own install base), 
2) Lack of growth opportunities for senior technical talent
3) Leaders don't want to hear tough messages, and disconnected from technical reality

Pros: Cisco cares about their employees and the world we live in, love my role within Corporate Communications and feel fortunate to have landed such an awesome job. Over a year in and I have no complaints.
Cons: Any cons I can think of are so minor, innovation and change in a large company can take a while, but I don't think that issue is unique to Cisco.

Pros:
The brand value matters the most. Best in computer networking industry. 
Lots of facilities for employees. WFH reimbursement upto INR 25K. Monthly home broadband reimbursement upto USD 350 (350 * equivalent INR conversion rate)
Cons: Most of the projects are in old legacy technologies (switching BU) running for more than a decade. Work pressure is always hectic. Even if they provide recharge day (intended to give much needed break to the employees), actually the team members end up doing extra work on the remaining days of the sprint to compensate the recharge day.

Pros: Lot of opportunities to learn, decent work life balance, management is friendly and understanding, less politics per my experience etc
Cons: Low salary for people who have been loyal to the company and staying here for long. Switching to multiple roles only can increase your package. No market correction procedure in place.

Pros: Work life balance is fantastic, run-rate will have you consistently paid, it's easy to shine when such a large populace of the sales team is pre-retirement
Cons: product-market fit is getting weaker and weaker, comp plans are getting more complex to curb massive payouts, you will only sell commoditized products (no disruption, no transformation).

Pros: Great brand and reputation, industry leader, bright people, excellent opportunities to learn, generous tuition reimbursement, a lot of freedom as long as you get the job done, strong executive mgmt
Cons: With size comes bureaucracy, do not expect annual salary increases,  as a global company many demands on work/life balance, in general very weak and inexperienced management at the director level, too much politics for a company that is trying to change the world

Pros: Top tier high tech company. The company as a whole treats their employees very well and has great benefits. The CEO, John Chambers, has great vision and heart.
Cons: Life and work balance is out of whack. The company expects you to be working whether you are on a vacation or it's a holiday. Everything is about the number you make and you feel like you are just part of the shuffle.

Pros:

* Every so often, cutting edge tech

* They turn off half the lights in the buildings
* Middle management is expanding

Pros: Not many...but still some good people there
Cons:
Very political company now

How a company like Cisco can have $30B in cash, not give even minimal cost of living raises and reduce benefits regularly and be considered a great place to work is beyond me...

Management treats employees like idiots and HR provides a playbook about how to answer employee questions, so no matter which organization you go to - you get the same answer.

Pros:
About as stable as it can be
Work from home
