Decreasing benefits (health, food, drinks, etc. - some big items, some small)
Food (used to be good)
A lot of people on cruise control until things pick up..then they will leave the company
Too much red tape
No travel - non-HQ teams/member cannot meet. If you are not in San Jose, you are at a major disadvantage
Too many corporate initiatives - can't keep track
Loosing its luster on the resume
Too big

Pros: Job security, benefits, visibility of the company in the industry, ability of the company to influence the way internet is built, innovation and thought leadership
Cons: More like a public sector, growth potential and associated opportunities don't come by so easily. There is a gap between the executive management and mid level management. Energy does not flow through all levels in the company

Pros: technology leader, mgmt supports with family and balance between work and personal life, WFH option, great place for ppl with lots of people skills
Cons: for a very good engineer it might take lot more effort than a person who is good with ppl skills.. hiring standards are bad.. might have to face and work in below average engineers sometimes.. unfair promotion, recognition and appraisal

Pros:
- A huge company with many opportunities
- Some of the smartest people in the world
- Best way to join Cisco is through an acquisition
- If you are smart, you can be successful even with average work. Depending on type of job, position, and business unit.
- Promotions can take a very long time, unless you have a senior-manager or VP godfather, or you accomplish an outstanding and disruptive project and get noticed by executive management.
- Job security
Cons:
First of all let me say that there is a huge variety of very different experiences in different BU, and across different job functions, so my review might not represent an entire organization. Also, many of the 'negative' aspects are found in probably any organisation of this size.

- A very political organization where you can find people care more about their position than their job duties.
- Senior accountability often not seen. The company is aware and is trying to change that.
- Can be very aggressive as you move up in management positions with many A-type aggressive managers. Can lead to conflicts of interests and internal competition.
- Stanford MBA management style, however not really as open as it might appear on the surface and criticism is not accepted well.
- You could find yourself 'lost', unappreciated, and unsupported if you have a bad manager (who could otherwise be brilliant and a nice person). I have seen it happen several times.
- It will take you much longer to move ahead and progress your career if you are working in an office remote from the main office where your BU management sits. Even with growing use of conferencing and TelePresence. Especially if there is a major time zone difference.

Pros: Exciting products and technology. Leader in its industry. Strong CEO. The quality of people is outstanding. High pride in the company. Sincerely tries to be a great employer. When focused, we can do anything we want.  Track record of performance as a company is remarkable.
Cons: Decision making can be slow.  A mix of leading-edge technology and out-dated practices (no longer a startup).  Complex coordination internally - many stakeholders to manage.  Don't come in with an entitlement mentality!

Pros:
Very good salary package
Great people to work with
Exposure to lots of interesting technologies
Lots of flexibility around working from home or remotely
Cons:
Far too much politics
No decision making process or collective decisions which are typically the worst that could be made
Lack of responsibility on decision makers
No sense of direction
Lack of focus

Pros: If one is looking to work in a large scale and highly complex system development, cisco is not a bad place
Cons: Too slow and highly inefficient. Many processes are archaic, boring and outdated. Politics play the most influential role at almost all divisions across the company

Pros:
1. Good innovative products. 
2. Flexible work hours. Even if you work for 5 hours a day, no issues. 
3. Good transport facilities at affordable cost. 
4. 10 % of the people you meet are "REALLY BRILLIANT".
Cons:
1. Very Bad mid-level managers. They just play politics and destroy people's career. 
2. Very poor hikes given. You should be prepared to get NO hike for 2 years.
3. Your immediate manager is GOD for you. If he turns a spoilsport, then you are doomed.

Pros: you may have opportunities to work on some really challenging works.  The products are complex enough, and also have been under development for many years.  if there are any unresolved issues assigned to you, it must be tough problem, then you got the chance to show your capabilities.
Cons:
Most of your time will be spent on porting existing code from one platform to another platform.  tedious and boring.

salary not increased every year.

Pros: Some of the best reasons to work at Cisco Systems India are; the talent you get to work with, great infrastructure, support for work-life balance, and an open culture that tolerates airing of opinions.
Cons: Unfortunately not everyone is open and honest, things tend to get political with people more interested in protecting their turf than getting on with the job at hand.

Pros: Great brand name and experience you can later leverage.
Cons: Easy to get lost and the best performers aren't always noticed.  It's not what you know but who you know kid!

Pros: Great benefits and work flexibility.
Cons: If you care about what you produce in life, and have grand goals in participating in some of the great technology innovations of our time, this is not the place to be.  The culture is sales driven; not technology driven.  The business units are constantly competing with each other internally and it is difficult to get anything done.

Pros: Cisco is a terrific place to learn about new technologies and to sharpen your resume.  The name carries a lot of weight.  There are a lot of really sharp people working there.
Cons: Management tends to play favorites and there are cliques of salespeople who have been around forever who seem to get the best accounts-and they are not always the hardest working AMs.  Sometimes corners are cut to get deals booked at the end of the quarter.  And the pressure to hit weekly goals is intense.

Pros: Good place to learn a lot
Cons: NO growth.Too political and need to be in the "inner" circle to get opportunities to grow.Managers themselves do nothing , but choose whom to keep ,or axe or assign projects.

Pros:
1) A lot of motivated, type A people intent on having an impact with the company and it's customers
2) Industry leadership garners respect for those who have succeeded at Cisco
3) Terrific attitudes about remote workers.
Cons:
1) Current transition of business model and tech focus is painful on employee base
2) Sales-driven company often drives focus on short term objectives
3) Annual lay offs have appeared to become a tradition

Pros: Great career and education opportunities; team collaboration, exposure to global markets and teams. Flexibility which is especially great for working mothers. Great culture; Cisco is big on giving so Philanthropy and Corporate Social Responsibilities are taken very seriously at Cisco.
Cons: Not much to say as far as Cons. Maybe there needs to be more concentration on the great products that Cisco produces so there is more of a push on those as opposed to new products who haven't reached the great market yet which don't have market share just yet.

Pros: Really good health coverage. Flexibility from working from home or in the office. Since Cisco has been doing better, they have started to encourage more sponsored social activities. Management says what you put in is what you get, but unless what you put in can be put into some sort of tool to be tracked, no one will notice.
Cons: There is a lot of "red tape" to do anything innovative. There is no experimentation. Even though working from home is an easy option to do, work life balance is dis satisfactory.

Pros: Great resources, compensation, and plenty of different roles to build a career around. Strong sales culture, innovative partnering and business development concepts.
Cons:
Top down strategy that is often ready-shoot-aim. There is a small circle of anointed ones who have a disproportionate ability to make decisions. Everyone else can say no, very few people can say yes.
Expectation of being always available. 60 hour weeks are the norm everywhere but in the EU.

Pros:
Great benefits
Competitive pay
Significant annual bonus (usually)
Huge company with serious brand recognition
Cons:
Too much work being done by too few people
Extremely tight deadlines
Too many incompetent engineers (in my group) with no repurcussions
Periodic "restructuring" affects morale and doesn't improve workload.
Lay offs usually affect employees based on project importance rather than employee merit
Huge company is difficult to manage
Most innovation comes from acquisition rather than internal invention

Pros:
Decent work life balance. People rarely work over 7-8 hours.
People work remotely and are still productive as they have the necessary tools.
Cons: The place is over staffed. Every year there are lay offs and all contractors are let go towards the end of the year with minimum impact to the projects or the work load.

Pros:
Incredible array of jobs - want a change, move to another role
Active use of collaborative technology
Has a active energetic can do culture - get it done
Is truly global
Cons:
Technology company so it must staying leading edge (can be a pro and Con)
Poor change management 
Moves quickly and that can be very disruptive to employees
Has shown tendency to create positions for senior execs when the positions may not make sense

Pros: Workload is low, you don't need to work hard to survive. Trainings are a lot, but your manager has to approve, so you can't take whatever classes you want
Cons: promotions are slow, take years, and not much of salary increase, you only can get some more bonus, but still far from average in bay area

Pros: Good Work life balance , Good exposure to technologies , Good work environment, Industry standard Salary ,  Additional benefits like transportation e.t.c , good organization structure, good cafetaria, Good infrastrcuture

Pros: Smart people, great friendships and some organizations are great to work for. Supportive in giving you the time off required and acknowledging the contributions made through achievement awards.

Despite exceeding expected performance goals consecutively each year, receiving acknowledgements and achievement awards for contributions and hearing of multiple promises of promotions over the years, my career growth has been non-existent.

Pros: Cisco allows for flexible hours and has a Good work life balance. It recently launched a paid paternity leave program
Cons: As any big company there is always the layoff threat as a response to stakeholders expectations or changes in the financial markets

Pros: Many architectures & significant acquisitions make it never a slow or dull place.  Pay is competitive.  Significant resources to draw upon.
Cons: Pace extremely fast.  Overlays  (PSS) do not control account deals.  New Exec team poised to take stock higher which can be good for stockholders & stressful for employees. Recently significant employee choice turnover.

Pros: High calibre of employees, good renumeration packages, exposure to a large corporation workings. Opportunity to progress internally is present if you desire this.

Some of the culture has eroded away over the years - working for Cisco is not considered as valuable as it was many years ago.

Pros: Virtual workforce makes for good work/life balance, compensation and benefits are fair, tools for collaboration and work are excellent, well respected brand

Because Cisco is a big company, you may have a lot of opportunities and works.

Because Cisco is a big company, you may not have dynamic works.

Pros: Strong forward thinking and strategic leadership.  Very talented and experienced teams.  Great collaboration and ability to execute.  A world class industry leader in Corporate Real Estate.

Pros: Cisco is a solid and reputable company that values its employees. Technology is always changing and Cisco continues to keep a pulse on the business and its employees. There are many opportunities for career and development growth as Cisco Management fully support this methodology.
Cons: As technology is always changing, it is sometimes a lengthy process to implement change as with any large company. However, it does get done through proper follow up, ownership and leadership.

Pros: Sales teams are very empowered and a strong opportunity to be creative and drive innovation. It's portfolio is impressive and provides a great opportunity to assist your customers.
Cons: The higher you go, you really start to see it's warts. It gets political quickly and many competing agendas really slow it down. It's multiple restructures has really hurt the collaboration, risk taking and moral.

Pros: Experience, technical expertise grow. There are some opportunities to work on different projects, but all for the price of your own time. CCIE certifications for free.

Pros: Great Colleagues, Good Culture, Ability to work in a global team in the true sense of the word, Stretch assignments that could be taken up based on aptitude and interest, management actively encourages job rotation
Cons: Highly matrix org structures, Dispersed teams, Constant changes can be a considered a con (if you are not up for it :)

Pros: Great team spirit, talented people, a lot of initiatives to participate and grow my network. I can improve my technical skills to better serve my customers. A lot of giving back activities so I can contribute and impact different communities.

Pros: I've never met anyone toxic at Cisco, and stress has been near-zero in my years here. Positive, upbeat vibe. We know what we are about, so do our customers, and we just have to do it well. Benefits are solid, I don't have to worry about the future.

Compensation is not as high as I could get at other companies.

Pros: Large portfolio of products to offer the customer, along with finance and advanced services options.

Advanced Services pricing not competitive with growing, higher-valued partner-offered services, forcing carve-out of profitable technical support services (TSS) instead.

Pros: Work culture, Task balancing, Work life balance, Work from home for some days  even before covid also, learning.
Cons:
less pay as per the brand name,
grade system is completely blank for new joinees sometime they hire more experience employees to low grade.

Pros: Cisco consistently paid on-time via direct deposit. The job did not require physical labor and the risk of injury was negligible.

Three years after I started, literally every person on the org chart between me and the CEO had left the company. I always had a job, but after the first few changes, I started to wonder if anyone's really steering the boat.

Pros:

Work/Life Balance
Company meet up and events
Ability to transfer positions or transition up
Worldwide known brand helps in your positioning against competitors

Business politics plays a big part of your personal success regardless of your numbers. The most qualified person isn't always the one who is rewarded. Seen this numerous times.

Toxic team sub-cultures, although you can work around this, just be aware it exists.

Pros: In the past, they have paid very well for performance. They give time to have a good work life balance and most managers our understanding and easy to work with.

Pros: We really are a company that cares about our customers and partners alike.  This has to be exemplified in the field of course, but Cisco gives us all of the tools and resources we need to show how much we care about our customers success as they build out their secure communications infrastructure.  Not to mention the GREAT job they have done at empowering the partners and really building a model that we can be proud of.  I came from a competitor 4 years ago that had a phenominal partner program and used to LOVE picking on Cisco's lack of partner friendly programs, resources and tools.  Now I can say that Cisco has really put great focus on that area and of course, there is room for improvement and nothing is ever ever perfect, but we are getting much closer.  The benefits that Cisco affords the employees are better when you are not in a remote territory, but they offer many other incentive programs that allow you to get the message that they care about employees well being.  I have watched this company go way above and beyond for many co-workers who have either lost a child due to illness, needed additional care for a cancer diagnosis, etc - that comes from the top and resonates throughout the entire organization.  We really work hard at living out our philanthropic duties in all of the countries that we serve through time, money and resources donations.  Again something that comes from the top.  We really are changing the way we work, live, play and learn!
Cons: There is never enough time in the day to get everything done that needs to get done.  Expectations are that we will try and live a balanced life, but that is very hard to do when the demands outway the time available!

Pros: Flexible work arrangements and use of Web2.0 are widely available and well adopted. It is fun to work with new technology

Pros: Work life balance can be good depending on the role and team you're on, good, collaborative team culture, advanced reporting systems, used to be more rotational opportunities in finance which allowed a diverse learning experience in finance

Pros: Great Salary, smart coworkers, remote work ok, "hoteling" office workspace isn't conducive to productivity for many job functions.

Pros: I am amazed at the number of talented individuals Cisco has managed to attract.

Pros: Cisco is not a start up anymore. It does have its fair share of politics, but the company as it is constantly acquiring new technologies and integrating some of them. You will always have some opportunity to learn and contribute.

Pros: Very flexible environment supports life work balance, established processes, infrastructure and use of technology enable productivity.  Intelligent people.  Progressive benefits like onsite health center and world class child care program. Truly a global organization.

Pros: Ability to learn new technologies. Ability to move into different areas of business. Policy allows transfers without interference of management.

Pros: Market leading products, world class engineers, and loyal customers.  The best product support in the industry, and the biggest reseller channel in the world.

Pros: Meaningful work, exposure to executives, great culture. Pros: Truly flexible work culture. Majority of meetings conducted virtually, means you can work from anywhere in the world, and that's actually OK. Work load is average overall, and team members and leaderships are very understanding different circumstances.

Pros: Positive successful organisation, good pay and benefits, great collaboration technology helps get business done, generally great people to work with in all countries I have experienced.

The pros probably are a cause of this since people stay a long time and new opportunities arise only from growth areas/organic growth in adjacent markets.

Pros: Great products, excellent working level teams, focused on winning.

Pros: Free onsite electric vehicle charging, great workout facility.

Pros: Flexibility, mobility, work - life - balance, diverse range of skills from technical to non technical

Pros:

Pros: Big Company , Lots of new stuff , good benefits

Focus on learning and personal growth

Pros: Fantastic technology, get to learn from some of the best people in the industry. Having Cisco on your resume will always mean something.

Pros: Agile company, even though large. Smart people and great winning and open culture. Great market leading portfolio, and strong company leadership

Pros: Currently top level leadership 100% "gets it". From the way they set the tone of culture to they way they focus on driving the areas of the business that truly matter, the top levels of management seem to truly be world class.

Pros: flexibility (work from home), really nice work culture even from upper management, lots of communication tools and free hardware (only wort-related), international network (offices everywhere), chance to attend big tech conferences (get to travel to US for work)

Pros: Commitment to excellence is high. At the same time work life balance is valued. So it's hard work but they don't expect everything from you and compensate well.

Pros: Conscious Culture at company helps us understand the importance of everyone being aware — “conscious” — of the environment they're part of, and feeling accountable, empowered, and expected to act in creating a culture where we feel safe and can thrive. Pros: Work with very talented and smart people in a multi-cultural environment. Cisco actually uses its own enterprise and collaboration systems within the company. The results is a dynamic and modern workspace using the latest technologies.

Limited job certainty as a result of regular restructuring. The logic behind who gets laid off is sometimes hard to understand.

Pros:

Pros: Good people culture, socially responsible, flexible working hours, and well set up for remote working. Lots of training options and good benefits. Some opportunities to travel to or work in the US. Employees generally get a good level or autonomy and opportunities to grow

Pros: Good salary and benefits. Higher level employment is very Agile oriented

Pros:

Pros: A lot of career opportunities and Cisco strongly encourages it's employees to look for advancement within Cisco. They take good care of their people.

Pros: Great work life balance and  Rey good compensation package

Pros: The culture fosters trust and respect. Flexible work hours allow employees work and life balance. Happy employees make a happier work environment, Start-up mentality encourages new ideas and approaches.

Pros: Brand name well respected in IT market. Quality products and solutions. Important edge versus competition. Continuously improving and innovating to cope with market demands and technology . Great work tools and facilities to support employees.

Pros: Industry leader, deep pockets with lots of challenging roles.  Can offer you a variety of roles if you do the work to grow your career at Cisco

Pros: Intelligent people.  Great, reliable bonus structure.  Visionary leader.

The culture I have seen elsewhere, where people look over their shoulders and wonder who's next is now present at Cisco.

Pros: The culture at Cisco is amazing.  Very relationship based  - with a high degree of respectful debate.  There is no shortage of great ideas, nor empowerment to execute on those ideas.

Pros: If you are able to hit the ground running on your first day and able to get through training quickly than this is the career for you.

Pros: Outstanding solutions, great extended team,flexible environment and well rewarded. Pros: Great benefits! There are lots of internal positions in San Jose.

Pros:

you are treated like a professional

Pros: Flexibility of working from home and work remotely when needed. Opportunities to work and collaborate with highly talented people, cross-functional team and geographically distributed team.

Pros: I was fortunate to work with a fabulous team under strong leadership.

Pros: Flexible working conditions, allowing working remotely, depending on your manager.  Most of the time, if you want to learn new skills, most managers will support your development.

Pros: The total compensation package is well above average in the tech industry.

Pros: The work culture and environment helps to get the best out of you. Really cares for their employees.

Pros: Innovation, compensation, camaraderie, most leadership, brand and reputation. Cisco sets a high standard for its employees. The smart people are really smart.

Pros:
Remote work environment 
Good benefits

Pros: Flexible, good pay, good benefits. If you are looking to sleep through life then this is a comfortable company.

Pros: Cisco offers a comparatively stable work environment with some very talented folks. There is a strong customer-oriented point of view across the company which has held up over the years.

Pros:
Being Part Of A Game-Changing Company made a great impact on my professional as well as personal life .mentoring and team building here inculcates strong team spirit values along with numerous opportunities to learn from our mentors.The strong work culture and diversity of people employed helps in our overall development as an individual .  And since

Pros: Great resources, lots of smart and talented folks. Good pay and benefits. A good company for younger workers who will be able to valuable experience in many areas.

Cons: Even though Cisco is moving the needle, diversity - on all levels - is still something that needs work.

Pros: Here is a gym on site that is cheap but good, work from home, employee purchase plan, great people, good opportunities

Pros: Lots of flexibility to control your time and manage work life balance...great for working parents, especially if both work full time. Great benefits which keep getting better, including paid family leave, backup home care, etc. Easy to move around within the company, job rotation is highly encouraged.

Pros: People, culture, empowerment, innovation, technology leadership

Pros: flexibility, work from home, work ethic, good pay

job was not as satisfying as initially promised.

many people who are fake friendly.

Great People, Culture and Diversity

 Tougher Work-Life Balance than many sales roles.

Pros: Cisco is an equal opportunity employer and networking giant to get exposure to lots of technologies. Great place to work for work/ life balance.

Pros: Cisco has a very easy and flexible work culture, great knowledge sharing and great place to work.  Gives a lot of flexibility.

Pros:

Pros: Was a rewarding job, great people, great talent.  Can accomplish great strides with the resources available.  Excellent benefits, people and work environment.

Pros:

Pros: The people were amazing, the culture was encouraging and motivating, the projects were challenging and created a collaborative environment to work in, and there were many training options to grow in your position.

Pros:

Bad/Less Hikes

Pros: Freedom to be innovative and creative,  cross functional across all Cisco not just silo'd into one group of people.  lots of new tech to get involved in.

Pros:

- Politics can stifle progress

Pros: John Chambers has created a dynamic and diverse leadership team that is focused on winning. Also, the company has such a broad set technologies and services that the TAM for Cisco is massive. Couple these things with a large cash position and a decent stock dividend and you get a company that is going to be hard to beat from a tech and financial perspective.
Cons: It's a huge company! Sometimes it is hard to navigate the organization and understand who is doing, or responsible, for what.

Pros: Good salary, the bonus is nice (when it applies) and work flexibility.  Depending on the job but the ability to work from home with a corporate router and phone. Decent benefits for medical and dental.  Free onsite gym.

Pros: Interesting and very flexible position, similar to a Customer Success Management in the SaaS world.  One can gain access to senior management at both the customer and Cisco.  Each individual defines his/her own scope of work.

Pros: A big company where you can rather easily move round for different opportunity. You will feel quite differently at different part of the company, maybe due to all the acquisitions over time

Pros: Some departments are great and empower their employees to lead projects, take charge and reward them appropriately. Pros: Flexible working arrangements, collaborative atmosphere, great benefits and culture.

Pros: coworkers are fantastic and very supportive.

Throw someone under the bus attitudes

Pros: Upper management is relentlessly positive. Potentially high level of team interactivity

Pros: Excellent flexibility, HealthCare Coverage, some sites have on-site medical & gym access.  One of the reasons I enjoy going to work is getting to interact and solve complex problems with truly brilliant minds.

Pros: Worked for Cisco Chennai which is very different from Cisco Bangalore in terms of culture and openness but had a chance to do some really interesting technical stuff

Pros: The culture is inclusive, and the people are great. I enjoyed the time I worked at Cisco, and would love to return. The giveback days are amazing, and allowed me to spend time in my community doing things to really make an impact.

Pros: Cisco is a great company to work for. Super friendly, they are commited to what they do, support a lot internal promotions and growth and pay very well! Pros: The overall compensation is very nice.   The work is interesting if you have not worked on network equipment before.

Pros: Great benefits and great flexibility. Exciting challenges.

Pros: Pays reasonably, decent benefits, in the city, nice office, some decent products, and a well recognized name on your resume.

Pros:
Reading many of the other reviews I can't agree more with the comment that as with any large company your experience will vary greatly from group to group.  As a senior manager I get a bit more exposure to the behind the scenes than many of the other posters.  Some of the positives:

- Ability to balance work/life - From my experience the lack of work/life balance is largely self inflicted when it occurs.  It's also far from universal.  I have had zero problem ever with taking time off.  Making my weekends my own and shutting down after I go home.  Based off of the empty parking lots in Boxborough and San Jose after 6:00 at night there are many others who have the same experience.

- Ability to communicate upward honestly - I'm not only encouraged but absolutely required to communicate up to my director the real state of things.  He doesn't want things sugar coated he wants to know the real state of things.  When there are problems he trusts me to handle them and to escalate when I need help. Then he provides it.

- Attempt at a fair rating rankings process -  Every attempt is made to assure that the twice a year ratings/rankings process is done fairly.  In my organization every manager is required to be able to justify in detail their stack ranking of employees.  We then go through a laborious process to merge the stack rankings across the managers.  While from an outside perspective it can seem like people aren't being rewarded from an internal perspective the reality is we have a highly talented and competitive workforce.  Most of the employees fit into the "Core" grouping.  The core grouping are people that are very good at their jobs but not "excelling".

- Renewed investment in College Hires.  Cisco has a major initiative going on for the past 2 years to hire both interns and full-time candidates.  This includes a fantastic sponsorship program for H1 students which employees them outside of the US if they don't make it through the lottery.  They are employed outside the US until they can be eligible for an H3 or other means of coming back into the US.  That's as good as any company can offer.
Cons:
That being said Cisco isn't perfect.  Far from it.
Ratings Rankings -  It's simple math.  If you stack rank your employees you can always identify a top 10% and a bottom 5%.  That doesn't mean that the bottom 5% are employees you want to get rid of or who are not good at their jobs.  

More than a few people focused on their careers to the exclusion of all else - Of course not only a Cisco problem but with the driven type A people we hire there are many that will stop at nothing to advance careers. 

Ratings Rankings at odds with teamwork - When you know you are going to be ranked against every member of your team you are not incented to make your teammate look good at your expense even if it's the right thing for the company.

Pros:
Nice package when you get laid of. Good benefits.  They know how to grow the company. No value for meritocracy. You can hang around without as long as you can get along. Excellent sales team, can sell any crap. Has a Good acquisition engine. No fear  of lay-off. 
Stable company. John chambers is God !!
Cons:
Too political, Highly inefficient. Lot of buerocracy.  Lack of innovation. Too slow . Lack of recognition.
Too Big.

Pros:
- Real recognition from upper management
- Smart, technical hard working co-workers
- Real team environment
- Great place to work if you like the flexibility to work from home and the office
- Great benefits even for contract employees
Cons:
- 24 hour work environment can be a killer
- Very hard to find your way up the ladder
- Seems impossible to convert contractors to full-time employees

Pros: great highly knowledgeable people to work around.  You get a lot of responsibility at any grade level.  Making a larger positive impact to the world.
Cons: mgrs are not trained enough to manage properly.  Promotions, evals, and raises are fairly political and current projects get most of the recognition.

Pros: This is a very stable company and a good future ahead being the leader in most of the products in market from Cisco.
Cons: The growth in career and growth in development of self can be slow. Not much atmosphere for innovative thinking, though it is appreciated by the management.

Pros:
- Good overall environment
- Voice of employees is heard
- Good exciting projects
- Excellent bonus the year Cisco do good
- very relationship oriented
- Flexible hours
- Excellent facilities for virtual meetings, and distributed workforce
Cons:
- Very stagnated at top - very difficult to get promotion
- Not rewarding people who are thought leaders 
- Very stressful environment

Pros:
1) Stock Options offered through acquisition. Best opportunity to acquire company stock at attractive price.
2) Modern campuses.
3) Exposure to technology.
Cons:
1) Management instability. (3 different managers assigned to our group in less than 6 months and I never met one of them).
2) Questionable ethics.
3) Big company running on auto pilot.

Pros: The large size of the company provides for much opportunity for growth and learning. I was able to transfer through the organization several times in my years there to continue to learn new areas of my job. Never got bored.
Cons: Hard to balance work and family. Political. Easy to get lost if you don't do something to stand out. All in all, not much bad things to say.

Pros: Good place for lazy experts talking and relaxing. People there could easily have big impact on other startup business. Junior engineers could get well trained there with plenty of time.
Cons: Not good for people who would like to get motivated, promoted, and innovate new things. Everything new is slowly picked up there. Traditional big company culture.

Pros: relaxed environment. stable job. good if u want to lead an ordinary existence and do the whole start a family and work thing your whole life without ambition for much else
Cons: very little growth potential. executive alignment is a mess. too much bureaucracy and a lot of penny wise pound foolish bs going on.

Pros:
Hard working employees focused on getting job done in collaborative fashion
Good communication and transparency from senior leadership
Opportunities for challenging and interesting work projects
Employees treated with respect; Company shows strong interest in employee welfare/well being
Cons:
Big and complex company makes cross functional decision making difficult and slows execution
Ongoing organizational structure churn has created unnecessary distraction

Pros: Good work and recog from mid-level managers and my direct manager. Work is self starting, freedom to go and pursue initiatives I feel benefits our clients.
Cons: Red tape, easy to get overlooked if not always giving extra effort, sometimes overworked in services (not sure about engineering divisions). Easy for others to "cruise" but also easy to stand out if you put in the effort.

Pros: Resources is unlimited in the networking world, delegating responsibilities towards others is achievable here. Working from the bottom up is a far reach for those whom hope to succeed at Cisco.
Cons: Promotions are as rare as a Dodo Bird, management needs to stop hiring 3rd party consultants and help their current employees excel in the company.

Pros:
Work/Life Balance is good
Flexible work options
Co-workers
Cons:
Too much middle management
Hard to get promoted - no control over your career path
Difficult to move across organizations
Stock options are worthless

Pros: Everyone drinks the cool-aid and wants to win.  Cisco does a great job of listening, but at times has trouble putting the feedback into actions. Management has put rewards in place, the highlight the outstanding performances.
Cons: The constant changes in the sales force leads to limited continuity over a 2 year period.  Limited budget makes it difficult to do our job effectively.

Pros: Relaxed workplace with very flexible work timings and easy going culture. Decent salary
Cons: Very hierarchical could do better in the innovation department, sometimes communication from the top management is distorted. Some managers (not all) may not be open in giving proper feedback and help you get ahead in your career

Pros:
Flexible work schedule and place
Strong compensation package
Good opportunities to move around into different areas of company
Cons:
'Over' collaboration leads to slow and painful decision making process
Too many instances where employees that are 'bad' for the larger group are not dealt with appropriately

Pros: a lot of technologies to work on. only place to get access to so much knowledge about the industry and products - almost impossible to imagine this outside the company.
Cons: very conservative and territorial senior management. lack of clarity in executive communication. sometimes get a feeling that the executives and the individual contributors work in different companies.

Pros: Schedule flexibility.  Depends on the nature of your job, however from my experience, I've been able to achieve a successful career and still be present for the afterschool and in-class activities, sicknesses and other situations where a typical "in-office" 8-5 job would not allow.
Cons: Tyring to achieve a job change within a different organization within the company can be challenging.

Pros: Typically work with qualified and fun colleagues on sales opportunities. Can be a fast-paced environment depending on your job role. Overall the management does a pretty good job and the benefits are comparable to other companies in the area
Cons: It's a large company, so some amount of bureaucracy is to be expected. It's not nearly as bad as some of the other companies I've experienced, but it does exist.

Pros: Cisco took good care of its employees and contractors.  Flexible work hours, telecommute, plenty of parking, reasonable prices in their cafeterias.  Good perks.
Cons: Politics.  Lots of politics.  It shouldn't be a surprise.  Lack of job opportunities for contractors to find internal jobs or be promoted to full time.  Only a few of the contractors I knew were converted to full time.

Pros:
Work/life balance - flexibility to work wherever, whenever

Great Compensation- if you preform well, they definitely reward you

Working with exceptionally bright people

Work environment is clean and fresh (no more cubicles)

Benefits - many on campus perks (SJ)

Innovation is encouraged and rewarded
Cons:
There are definitely some old timers at Cisco that can be stuck in old ways of doing things

Problems you get with any large company 

Can be political and difficult to get raises/promotions, especially when the company isn't doing well

Pros: People are friendly, comparatively slow pace. Instructions are clear. Great perks and the teams go out to do activities every month or every 2-3 weeks or so, which is covered by the company.
Cons: It's a big corporation, so you may be working at a position for years and not move up. But it's typical for such a giant.

Pros: Work culture in Cisco as a global company is good. Work and work life balance is decent.
Cons: Recognition and compensation are not based on merit. Culture in Cisco India has changed very much due to rapid expansion. Local management is not effective and hence teams are not productive enough to justify the costs to company. Talent and people are not valued.

Pros: Cisco is going out in new fronts. I am currently in IoE field and product is more than interesting. Great team, training catalog, work-life balance.
Cons: Core products under attack by competitors and self-degradation.

Pros: Good work, great people, flexibility, challenging work, great customers and visibility.
Cons: Constant changes in direction, compensation stays stuck where you first started, arcane performance review process. Self promoters do well at the expense of those who actually contribute.

Pros: flexibility to work from home, good work/life balance
Cons: they keep cutting in the wrong places,  no room for growth, constant layoff's and restructuring. getting ahead is all about who you know NOT what you actually contribute. they "grade" you on a bell curve and good/strong performers are pushed into the bottom b/c "someone has to be in the bottom".

Pros:
Variety of products and services, Cisco has a lot to offer customers and significant opportunity for employees.
Growth in data center and cloud phenomenal.
John Chambers is a tremendous leader.
Great channel network.
Cons:
Who is going to lead company in the future and will they be able to be as visionary and great leader as John Chambers?
Lack of consulting services leadership and staff.

Pros: Flexibility (remote worker), international culture, paycheck.
Cons: Cisco is becoming a cheap company, everything has to be done via ticket/cases, processes and organizations are changing all the time making it an unsecure environment. If you are not based in one of the key "low cost" locations you career opportunities will be very limited as new jobs are only open in those cheap locations (RTP, Krakow, Dalian, India).

Pros:
Always work to be done
Great ability for work-life balance if you don't mind being on calls all the time
Cons:
- Tough to deliver meaningful successes in a short timespan
- Career growth predicated on proving yourself through deliverables...since it takes forever to deliver, expect real growth to take a long time
- Building consensus through meetings ise more important than actually getting work done

Pros: Everyone is extremely friendly and the corporate culture is great.  Everyone that I have interacted with are very intelligent hard workers.  Management pushes for personal development and I feel that I'm learning and growing every day.
Cons: The age gap... a lot of older folks work here so if you are young you need to work a little bit to find a group.

Pros: The base salaries are good. The work is dynamic and if an employee doesn't like his/her current project, managers do help in getting them the right work. There are some excellent development opportunities given to the new graduates. Work Life balance is good. New Office setting looks amazing.
Cons:
- No Stock Options
- Environment is a little dull. Less interaction between the employees.
- Less energetic

Pros: New CEO and Exec mgmt are moving fast to pivot with cloud, software and services.  Chuck and the leadership team will move the company to the top IT player in the world
Cons: May be shifting a little late but team is great that is in place.  Cisco has a great portfolio and is fine tuning it

Pros: It's a good place to work for you if you are a beginner. Colleagues are friendly and open to ideas. Lots of opportunities to learn.
Cons:
There is no salary increase. The management never cares about the salary increase of the existing employees though they are outstanding.
Old style management. Needs to be completely revamped.

Pros:
Fast-paced environment that can be very motivating
Leading edge technology vision and portfolio
Very customer focused
In process of flattening the organization to move quickly
Cons:
People deal is not authentic to actions taken by leaders
Seems more political than necessary
Strategy in flux; clinging to old hardware/product focus
Many experienced and valuable leaders have departed

Pros:
work life balance is good
work from home can make it flexible
good facilities and benefits
Cons: I won't recommend Cisco if you are on H1B. They will keep doing layoffs and they will be unable to file your PERM. Pay is not so great. Small or non existent pay raises

Pros: Company has lots of different technologies to pick from. If you have the opportunity to get in, it's a great place to start a career, but with the intention of leaving 1-2 years into the job.

Pros: leading edge R&D, contribution to open source is welcome, good compensation, stock options, additional days to vacation, friendly environment, best professionals always willing to help, splendid working place

Pros:
The new CEO is transforming the company to the better

Very good pay
Innovation
Well run

Not growing and with that very limited upward mobility for experienced employees
Transition to an as a service and SW company is complex and drives a lot of churn

Pros: Good benefits, diverse working environment, many opportunities to move within the company.

Pros:

Diverse environment, colleagues from all around the world
Work from home, flexible policies
exposure to Cloud and Agile methodologies
Large scale and ability to invest
lots of training available
great potential

Big corp trying to shift into an higher gear:
frequent change in strategies, tools, methodologies
yearly reorgs
yearly redundancies
outsourced functions (eg HR, asset management) very process-oriented and mindless in their approach
clueless Product Managers

Pros: Flexibility, inclusive, fun activities,  respectful and collaborative environment, innovation. Compared to lot of other companies, Cisco has a variety of events and activities to engage people from all culture and generations.

Pros: Having Cisco on a resume isnt a bad thing, because people that see your resume that also worked there know you are survivor of ITs Auschwitz.

Cons: With the company being so large and constantly acquiring new companies there is always a lot to learn. Which is also sometimes a Pro.

Pros:
Flexible work week, work from home options.
Challenging work, talented people. 
Opportunities to make a difference in the industry.
Huge careers potentials with the right manager.

Pros:
1. Rub shoulders with industry bigwigs.

3. Travel opportunity to learn from the experts in San Jose, CA.
4. Flexible work environment.
5. Availability of massive learning resources

1. A bit unstructured in terms of the processes involved.
2. Being open to do a bit of grunt work once in a while.

Pros:
- Work Life balance
- Work environment
- Great campus and workspace

Pros: The people are amazing and make you look forward to coming to the office. Cons: Sometimes work can be overwhelming and consume a lot of time and it is often times challenging to find that work life balance/integration.

Pros:
organized, ethical, mature, flexible, 
sense of team work, team building, partnreship.

Pros:

- Work anywhere technology
- Good benefits

- People not hired based on merit

Pros:

- Donation matching
- Focus on employee wellbeing
 - Onsite health center and daycare
 - Good food onsite with a loving food staff
 - Intentionally seen during COVID-19 (the ELT has weekly calls focused on lifting spirits checking in on employee wellness)
- Strong work from home culture
Cons: "Cisco layoffs" are notorious but typically employees are given the opportunity to find new jobs internally

Pros: Lets us build better post solution deployment affinity with the customers. We can see their challenges from their lens and help them overcome the technology adoption barriers. This speeds up the technology usage and adoption and helps the customer to love Cisco solutions.
Cons: Sometimes the lack of telemetry data becomes a hurdle in assessing health of solution at customer premises but Cisco is striving hard to overcome this gap by building cloud links of solution to collect proactive telemetry data.

Pros: Good company to have a career. Since it is a horizontally wide company with so many jobs, the experience may vary, however in general if you are a software engineer or QA, you will find enough room to grow vertically.

Pros:
Great company culture
One of the best IT/networking companies a professional can work for
Benefits are great
In person internship experience was good
Cons: Very high expectations for a new graduate early in career, who is located remote. Manager had almost 20 reports and barely met with me or supported me properly. It’s unfortunate because the company itself is amazing, my internship was great, but really poor experience.

Pros: Love my team, the have-your-back culture. Competitive pay, excellent benefits (paid time off, medical leave, maternity and more), dental, medical, 401k. Work from home, remote, relatively flexible work hours. Opportunity to grow and move around to fit your goals and skill set. Your hard work is recognized and rewarded, and the company (and coworkers) is behind you when you're in a bind and need support. Amazing company!
Cons: I really can't name any right now... I do miss being in an office!

Pros: - Great benefits with stock options - The company offers a lot of different support benefits even outside of working hours, like travel support and emergency help. - Somewhat competitive salary. I say somewhat as it depends if what you do is in demand and how replaceable you are.
Cons: - Very little advancement opportunity unless you are in sales. - So much bureaucracy and unnecessary hoops to jump through for simple things sometimes.

Pros: Flexible work environment.  Part of a world-class company with strong ethics and employee empowerment.  Great options to explore opportunities in technology and leadership. It's a competitive and highly motivated work environment that is good for some but not everyone.
Cons: Sometimes the work - life balance is compromised by the motivated work environment.

Pros: Big company, easy to change jobs and even roles within the company. Has a health center and a Walgreens, which is very convenient for us the employees. Really good health care benefits.
Cons: Very burocratic... It is hard to get anything done when it comes to internal processes (buying equipment, etc).

Pros:
- Excellent support for working efficiently: laptops, workgroup software; telepresence; support for work from offsite
- Really sound business-savvy and business-conservative leadership at the top
- Work with smart decent people
Cons:
- Big place; hard to get a grasp of the company as a whole
- Not the best paid place to work

Pros:
1.Very helpful colleagues.
2.Good compensation .

5. The leading company in the networking industry.
6. Good innovations.

1. No feedback give to employees.
2. Location is not very good.
3. No rewards/bonuses.
4. Company is slowly getting down in terms of its new products and some products are being fetched back from the market which is incurring losses.

Pros: Great techonology very innovative breadth of portfolio in collaboration unmatched. Good balance of work and life. Market leadership in collaboration

Pros: Be part of a big team spread across multiple continents around the world. One of the few oldrst and original tech companies around.

Pros: Great place for work/life balance.  Relaxed environment with many opportunities.  Ability to do your job without micromanagement.  Highly recommended company.

Pros:
- there are good benefits, including a good daycare
- culture of open communication
- friendly and challenging work environment
Cons:
- promotions are slow to come
- stock keeps going down or stays low
- projects move slowly due to large siloed systems. takes a long time to bring alignment amongst groups in order to move a project forward.

Pros: Challenging work whe you are in the right group, many smart people
Cons: Too large of a company, can't move up unless our are in a circle of "friends". Upper mgmt is too thick, too many outsourcing of engineering jobs.

Pros: Flexibility, Open work culture and best in Industry. Cares much about the employees. Technical competency cannot be challenged. Industry leader in internet related technologies.
Cons: Too many market adjacencies to focus on that sometimes loses track on what the company should be focusing on and with what intensity.

Pros: Openness,  fairness and open exchange of information between cross-functional teams (SE's,  Business units and Sales force ) is very good.
Cons: SVP and Director level management are internally focussed.  Too many politics, and distracts from execution and clarity about long term strategy.

Pros: Great, awesome, hard-to-beat health benefits. This is not a sell if you are single, young and fit, but great family support and campus life works well.
Cons:
Small cog in a small team as part of a large team in some business unit whose name changes so regularly that one forgets and doesnt care.

Sometimes management dont trust engineers!

Pros: work-life balance is good. it is a very big positive
Cons: transparency is lacking and each man to his own

Pros: Flexibility in work hours and ability to work remote.  Decent benefits.
Cons: Incredibly difficult to get quick results.  Too many chiefs.  Politics still determine who succeeds, not the best performers.

Pros: They hire talented people, pay them well and give you great flexibility to set your schedule.
Cons:
There is nobody in the office. Everybody is "working" off-site and since they are not really working they are not avaible to help you or even respond to an email.
The mass layoffs are not done. Another set is loooming.

Pros: Latest technology that's driving present and future markets and networks. Very good compensation package and perquisites. Recognition and rewards is well integrated  into Cisco culture. Above all, flexible timing,  work from virtually any part of the world and a great employee education system makes Cisco a great place to work.
Cons: Petty office politics might bother you a bit, but never mind everything else over shades this down side.

Pros: So influential in the rise of the internet. Bellweather for tech.
Cons: Lots of layers. Executive leadership has been spotty. No clear strategy in many groups other than playing the best defense.

Pros:
Great IT infrastructure
Great on-line tools to help with every area of your job
People are always willing to help and go above and beyond
Cons:
Large bureaucracy can tend to delay decision making longer than normal
Seems like there was a re-org at the end of every fiscal year
Had troubles figuring out their core competencies. I think they finally have it right.

Pros:
1. Execution focused organization. Decent work-life balance.
2. Relationship building is key to be successful - truly the human network at play!
3. Employee friendly culture. Great benefits.
Cons:
1. A bit of top-down decision making. The firms' large size forces senior execs to bet only on mainstream trends (a liability for people who want fast moving careers).
2. Lot of presentation & meetings, in the name of collaboration, kills productivity compared to working in a startup/mid-size firm.

Pros: Started working at Cisco out of college about a year ago.  Great company to work for - a ton of resources and really love the team atmosphere.  Cisco is definitely coming back from the layoffs/re-orgs 2-3 years ago.
Cons: Every large company has their political problems but overall, Cisco is one heck of a company to work for, especially out of college

Pros: Compensation and career opportunities are there for those who want to contribute towards the growth and transformation of the company.
Cons: Large corporation has its pluses and minuses.  There is security against major economic downturns, individual influence and dollar impact is higher even at mid level in the organization.  Decision making is solid but takes a bit longer due to impact to many stakeholders.

Pros: One of the most successful and long lasting networking companies in the last 2 decades.  Great benefits and pay is very fair.
Cons: Decision making is slow and managers are not really empowered.  Not much innovation.  Most of the new products in new market segments come via acquisition.

Pros: Work on new technologies and equipment. Decent work/life balance, decent salary.
Cons: Yearly lay-offs. Seemingly little or no cohesion between BUs. The drive to push all engineering over to Bangalore.

Pros:
Very accomodative , understandigly management 
lot of flexibilty once you established yourself. Training opportunities are lot, Easy to roatate the job within the company. Very good company for working mothers .
Cons:
Less growth
Bonuses are not sure . Frequent Layoff . Lot of processes which kills the any innovation passion.

Pros: Great benefits, home office options, cash awards, great work environment and great people to work with. International opportunities are available if you know who to talk to. Engineers are high class and super smart.
Cons: Management can make some tricky decisions, finding a growth path can not be easy but if you know the right people you can definitely become a star here.

Pros: Flexibility, people you work with, pay, bonus & benefits, professional development
Cons: Management - If you get a bad manager, your life can be miserable, Very siloed organization leading to duplication at times; Lack of proactive strategic outlook for market transition - playhing catch up; No more stock options for individual contributors, legacy tools & ordering slowing down TTM / impact customer satisfaction

Pros:
Learning from experts (You will find top software engineers in your team)
Access to latest network technologies
Relatively good compensation package
Flexible work environment
If you choose the good teams, you will find nice managers and co-workers. Really enjoy hanging out with fellow peers
Cons:
Switching to Agile, but in the wrong way
Sometimes they hire idiots
Salary growth not good, especially when you know people joined recently make more money
Lack of career opportunities, because we have 60k of employees....
Too many levels of management
Layoffs: literally once a FY

Pros: Great pay was the only benefit I saw at Cisco.
Cons: They talk work life balance, but it isn't practiced.  Manager would say he doesn't check/write email on weekends and then would ask me if I read his email from over the weekend.  Went on vacation and the same thing happened.

Pros: Good salary, plenty of opportunity to change positions, and plenty of support from management for growth.    Managers are mostly hardworking and competent.    Benefits are good.   Gym available at many sites.
Cons: Constant change, and regular broad-based layoffs.   Work is around-the-clock and never stops.    Top-down culture can mean having to commit to the impossible, and then explain the failures later

Pros: Cisco used to be a great innovative company in the late 90's and first half of previous decade

Salaries are no longer competitive in industry
Too many managers, VP's, directors and too little customer facing sales and engineers
process driven company; by average you spend about 30-40% of your time on admin related work (forecasts, deal approvals, discounts, etc)
Turning into a very large non-agile company
Career options are very limited

Pros: Networking giant and by working for them you learn an incredible amount about networking and the tech industry. Great place to launch a career.
Cons: Sometimes it feels like the work you do is insignificant due to the sheer size of the company. Incredibly difficult to move up the corporate ladder. Culture is pretty stiff.

Pros: Cisco is a great place to learn, rack certifications, and grow both technical, soft, and business skills. And then move on, vertically or sideways.
Cons:
It's a bureaucracy, with petty office politics.

It's easy to get buried under work there.

You won't get a promotion unless you know the right people, and are on the right projects (advancement is earned more from visibility rather than merit.)

Pros: Excellent infrastructure. One of the best in BLR. Strong talent pool - both technical and leadership.  Vast opportunity as virtually every business function and every technology is represented in Cisco India.
Cons: Yearly layoffs, feeling that one is playing a survival game and competing with one's peers. Compensation could be better...

Pros:
Investment and focus on innovation makes it an exciting place to work.
Culture from top management of respecting individuals flows down and across the company.
Cons:
Many managers lack the management skills to truly develop their teams. Company has the people process but not a culture that promotes excellence in management of people.
Too much of the innovation investment and energy is wasted. Don't always see the tangible results delivered.

Pros: The culture allows one to work independently.  The company provided great training opportunities throughout my career there.  Overall great company.
Cons: It is often very stressful working at this company.  It seems that promotions do not always go to the most qualified or best suited person.

Pros: Great Tech, Great People, good bonus, good ESPP, and good benefits.

Pros:
- Steady paycheck
- Benefits (though slightly below-average) 
- Good at leveraging market dominance for quick profit
- Salesman/marketeer paradise (engineers bane)
Cons:
I've spent more than a decade and a half working at Cisco trying to improve quality:

- *Nothing to offer an innovative, competent, honest engineer who's looking to effectively apply their hard earned technical skills* If you take pride in your work, look elsewhere. CIsco's so-called "collaborative" environment  focuses primarily on CYA tactics dominated by political motivations to manipulate image. In these meetings you'll see discussions center around how to make project "look good" and how to hide issues that "look bad". No discussion or activity on doing the right thing for customer and for quality of product(s).
- *Cheapest solution is synonymous with best solution* With such low skilled engineering and management talent in place there is no understanding of common processes such as trade-off analysis between quality of work, time and cost. You are expected to produce the quickest, cheapest solution under all circumstances as long as it looks good on a slide when presented to execs. This is culturally pervasive throughout the organization.
- *Impossible to exert influence* Staff and management are so unsophisticated about the industry and market realities that they don't even know what they don't know. There is no possible way to influence in this type of environment. Your years of finely honed technical skills and field experience carry no weight among the myriad of sales and marketing execs who can't think beyond the current quarter. Short-term sales goals trump every argument under all circumstances.
- *Poor quality work is rewarded* The formula for success is say "yes", do poor work, hide tracks, wait for next re-org, get promoted. There is no follow up on effectiveness or quality of work - ever. You are simply measured on how quickly you get a task done and how well you "make yourself look and your boss look" for quarterly ops reviews. If it looks good on a single power point slide, then it is good - reality is nothing.
- *Factory worker mentality* Management overly obsessed with the adage "if you can't measure it, you can't manage it". With marketing and sales dominating executive ranks, the metrics used to measure performance are nothing short of comical. Not only are such metrics easy to manipulate through unproductive activity but often encourage adversarial internal relationships (for example, tester performance evaluated positive on bugs found per week and developer performance evaluated negative on same metric). This makes managements job easy when it comes time to rank and lay off employees but severely hurts product quality, employee moral and the corporate bottom line.
- *Unrealistic expectations* Other than sales opportunities, execs are years behind in product deployment strategy and customers quality requirements. Execs haven't a clue what it takes to roll-out production ready products and continually ignore people who know and can prove otherwise. As a result, engineers are expected to make up difference in totally absurd time frames and that can only be achieved  by producing poor quality work. And if you don't meet expectations, you will hear about it next review.

Pros:
*Large number of Career Opportunities in different Business Units, Locations, etc.
*Large # of Opportunities to switch positions or divisions within the company but you need to network and word hard like any other job hunting
*Strong benefits package
*Competitive salaries but they will never pay you the top top dollar
*Gave big bonuses when the company had a big year even while other Blue Chip Tech companies like Google were laying people off or asking people to take salary reductions
*Strong Senior Leadership & Strategy.
*Continually entering new markets and finding ways to make more money. The company is growing despite being so large.
*Work Life Balance is Great, but I've heard different things in different groups.
*Lots of smart talented people
*Opportunity to telecommute or work remote but usually needs to be negotiated up front
*Some decent perks but seem to be mainly only for SJ campus
Cons:
*Bell Curve Ranking of Top 10%, 25%, Middle, Bottom 10% often ends up ranking good people bad. BUT, they have made recent changes to minimize this
*Due to the Bell of the Top 25%, you could be a great employee (26th best out of 100 for example) and have a hard time getting a promotion or salary increase
*Matrixed organization often finds multiple people doing same job or similar things, Hard to completely own something on your own
*Great senior leadership doesn't always cascade down to your VP, Director, or Manager. A substantial # of Mgmt doesn't follow the same culture and objectives as the senior team
*Culture & Expectations can vary from organization to organization or from team to team. You really can't use one experience (even a positive one) to be indicative of another.
*Competitive salaries but they will never pay you the top top dollar.
*Not going to make it rich off any Stock Options in the short term
*Could be more "fun"
*No Free employee shuttle or sponsored shuttle from Fun San Francisco to Boring San Jose like most big tech companies in the Bay Area provide
*Acquired companies often don't get the same perks/advantages as those already fully integrated

Pros: The company was very supportive of the community.  They were always having a fundraiser or donation drive for some of the local charities.  They also supported the local STEM program.
Cons: Like many large companies, there is a tendency to sell of business units and lay off employess as a way to show improved bottom lines.

Pros: Cisco has a lot of resources on hand, a great place to learn and train. With a flexible culture, work-life balance can be achieved at the greatest level.
Cons: A lot of bureaucratic procedure, as of recent years, re-organisation is also a regular pattern.

Pros: Flexible on work hours and location. Good benefits like bonuses and training opportunities. Plenty of ways to get involved and contribute.
Cons: Raise and promotion process is too opaque and inconsistent. Tendency to over plan. Too many meetings is typical.

Pros: Good benefits package and salary
Cons: Such frequent shifts in management only shake things up for a short time (every 2-3 years) Many layoffs, difficult to work across Business Units. Getting a raise at Cisco is a rare occurrence, so get what you can up front.

Pros: Good Solid Company for Employees. Good Salary. Very Healthy. Cash rich. Leader in Market. Know and trusted by customers.

Pros: Great company to work for-- offers great benefits, a collaborative culture, and the company really cares about their people.  The finance team really encourages employees to move around within Cisco finance to gain a better knowledge of how things work.

Pros: Get to work with the best of the best; enterpreneurial work spirit; very flexible - work from anywhere; well compensated with numerous benefits
Cons: Zero job stability; people get cut regardless of being high performers; countless number of layoffs targeted by business areas

Pros: Because Cisco is the king of collaboration, you can get your job done essentially anywhere. Access to many offices. Decent work/life balance (at times)
Cons: I would not recommend Advanced Services. We often have to deal with thousands of Sales People. Management and Senior leadership tends to be quite out of touch from the top down. Very difficult to grow.

Pros: The culture at Cisco is really awesome.  They offer many benefit choices for all stages of life.  Cisco continues to provide great programs to be involved with your family and community.
Cons: So far throughout my tenure at Cisco, I have not experienced any cons in my role.  The team is great to work with, my manager has a wealth of knowledge and an awesome coach.  Cisco is very transparent.

Pros:
Remote work and flexible hours in many roles
Great working tools
Friendly corporate culture
Working in the tech leader for market leaders

Managers are very automomous which can lead to HR policy abuse
Employees vs contractors
No fixed yearly pay rises (inflation compensation)

Pros: There is only positives working at Cisco.  How you are treated, compensated, and supported are top notch.  I have been in the work force since I was 13 and after 40 years of working with several different companies this is by far the best company I have ever worked for, and recommend all to join us.
